cards.ask: Imran is rich at home in Kufa, but he is robbed on a journey and is left with nothing. May he take zakat?
options: Yes: he is ibn as-sabil, a stranded traveller
No: he is rich at home
Only once he is home again
cards.source: وابن السبيل: من كان له مال في وطنه وهو في مكان لا شيء له فيه
cards.why: That is exactly the traveller: wealth at home, nothing where he is.

cards.ask: Sa'd collects zakat for the imam. He is not poor. What does he get from it?
options: Pay from the imam for the work he did
Nothing, because he is not poor
An eighth of all he collects
cards.source: والعامل: يدفع إليه الإمام بقدر عمله إن عمل
cards.why: The worker is paid according to his work, even if he is not poor.

cards.title: One kind is enough
cards.ar: وللمالك أن يدفع إلى كل واحد منهم وله أن يقتصر على صنف واحد ولا يجوز أن يدفع الزكاة إلى ذمي
cards.en: The owner may give to every kind, or give it all to just one kind. Zakat may not be given to a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule).

cards.ask: Fatima gives all her zakat to poor people and to no other kind. Is that allowed?
options: Yes: she may keep to one kind
No: she must split it among all eight
No: she must use at least two kinds
cards.source: وله أن يقتصر على صنف واحد
cards.why: The owner is free to give to just one kind.

cards.ask: Can this person receive zakat?
items: A mukatab paying for his freedom
source: والغارم: من لزمه دين
يعان المكاتبون في فك رقابهم
وابن السبيل
والمسكين: من لا شيء له
ولا يجوز أن يدفع الزكاة إلى ذمي
ولا تدفع إلى غني
cards.why: Debtors, mukatabs, travellers and the needy are among the eight. A dhimmi and a rich man are not.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: A faqir has a little; a miskin has nothing
The share of al-mu'allafa qulubuhum has dropped
"In the way of Allah" means fighters cut off from supplies
Zakat must be split among all eight kinds
Zakat may be given to a dhimmi

source: والفقير: من له أدنى شيء والمسكين: من لا شيء له
قد سقطت منها المؤلفة قلوبهم
وفي سبيل الله: منقطع الغزاة
وله أن يقتصر على صنف واحد
ولا يجوز أن يدفع الزكاة إلى ذمي
cards.why: The first three are right. One kind is enough, and a dhimmi may not be given zakat.

cards.title: Not for buildings or shrouds
cards.ar: ولا يبنى بها مسجد ولا يكفن بها ميت ولا يشترى بها رقبة تعتق ولا تدفع إلى غني
cards.en: Zakat may not be used to build a mosque, to buy a shroud for the dead, or to buy a slave to set free. It may not be given to a rich person.

cards.title: Not to close family
cards.ar: ولا يدفع المزكي زكاته إلى أبيه وجده وإن علا ولا إلى ولده وولد ولده وإن سفل ولا إلى امرأته ولا تدفع المرأة إلى زوجها عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: تدفع إليه
cards.en: You may not give your zakat to your father or grandfather (however far up), your children or grandchildren (however far down), or your wife. For Abu Hanifa a wife may not give hers to her husband. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say she may.

cards.ask: Mahmud has zakat to give. Where may it go?

options.text: A poor neighbour
A man weighed down by debt
His poor grandfather
His poor grandson
His wife
Building the village mosque

source: ولا يدفع المزكي زكاته إلى أبيه وجده وإن علا ولا إلى ولده وولد ولده وإن سفل ولا إلى امرأته
ولا يبنى بها مسجد
والغارم: من لزمه دين
cards.why: A poor neighbour and a debtor may receive it. Grandparents, grandchildren, a wife and a mosque may not.

cards.title: Slaves, a rich man's child, Banu Hashim
cards.ar: ولا يدفع إلى مكاتبه ولا مملوكه ولا مملوك غني ولا ولد غني إذا كان صغيرا ولا تدفع إلى بني هاشم وهم: آل علي وآل عباس وآل جعفر وآل عقيل وآل حارث بن عبد المطلب ومواليهم
cards.en: Not to your own mukatab or slave, a rich man's slave, or a rich man's young child. Not to Banu Hashim (the Prophet's ﷺ clan): the families of Ali, Abbas, Ja'far, Aqil and al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and their freed slaves.

cards.ask: Hadi is 9 years old and his father is rich. May Hadi be given zakat?
options: No: he is a rich man's young child
cards.source: ولا ولد غني إذا كان صغيرا
cards.why: A rich man's young child may not receive zakat.

cards.title: Giving by mistake
cards.ar: وقال أبو حنيفة ومحمد: إذا دفع الزكاة إلى رجل يظنه فقيرا ثم بان أنه غني أو هاشمي أو كافر أو دفع في ظلمة إلى فقير ثم بان أنه أبوه أو ابنه فلا إعادة عليه وقال أبو يوسف عليه الإعادة
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa and Muhammad: if you give zakat to someone you think is poor, and he turns out rich, a Hashimi or a non-Muslim, or you give it in the dark and he turns out to be your father or son, you do not pay it again. Note: Abu Yusuf says you must pay again.

cards.ask: Ziyad gives his zakat to a man, then finds out he is his own mukatab. Does it count?
options: No: all three imams agree it does not count
cards.source: أو مكاتبه لم يجز في قولهم جميعا
cards.why: Giving to your own mukatab does not count, in the view of them all.

cards.title: Anyone below a nisab
cards.ar: ولا يجوز دفع الزكاة إلى من يملك نصابا من أي مال كان ويجوز دفعها إلى من يملك أقل من ذلك وإن كان صحيحا مكتسبا
cards.en: Zakat may not go to someone who owns a nisab of any kind of wealth. It may go to someone who owns less, even if he is healthy and earns a living.

cards.ask: Rashid is healthy and has a job, but owns only 150 dirhams. May he receive zakat?
options: Yes: he owns less than a nisab
No: he is healthy and earning
cards.source: ويجوز دفعها إلى من يملك أقل من ذلك وإن كان صحيحا مكتسبا
cards.why: Owning less than a nisab is what counts, even for a healthy earner.

cards.ask: In the dark, Ilyas gives zakat to a poor man who turns out to be his own son. What do Abu Hanifa and Muhammad say?
options: It counts: he need not pay again
His son must hand it back
It counts only if he tells his son
cards.source: أو دفع في ظلمة إلى فقير ثم بان أنه أبوه أو ابنه فلا إعادة عليه
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa and Muhammad there is no repeat when the mistake is found out later.

cards.title: Sending it elsewhere
cards.ar: ويكره نقل الزكاة من بلد إلى بلد آخر وإنما تفرق صدقة كل قوم فيهم إلا أن ينقلها الإنسان إلى قرابته
cards.en: It is makruh (disliked) to send zakat from one town to another. Each people's zakat is given out among them, unless someone sends it to his relatives, or to people more in need than those of his own town.

cards.ask: Allowed, makruh, or not allowed?
items: Sending zakat to poor relatives in another town
Sending it to a town in greater need
Sending it to another town for no reason
Paying for a dead man's shroud
Giving it to a poor man of Banu Hashim
Giving it to a healthy worker below the nisab
source: ويكره نقل الزكاة من بلد إلى بلد آخر
إلا أن ينقلها الإنسان إلى قرابته أو إلى
هم أحوج من أهل بلده
ولا يكفن بها ميت
ولا تدفع إلى بني هاشم
وإن كان صحيحا مكتسبا
cards.why: Moving zakat is makruh unless it goes to relatives or the more needy. Shrouds and Banu Hashim are not allowed. A healthy earner below the nisab may receive it.

cards.title: Who pays it
cards.ar: صدقة الفطر واجبة على الحر المسلم إذا كان مالكا لمقدار النصاب فاضلا عن مسكنه وثيابه وأثاثه وفرسه وسلاحه وعبيده للخدمة
cards.en: Sadaqat al-fitr is the charity given for Eid al-Fitr, at the end of Ramadan. It is wajib on a free Muslim who owns a nisab's worth beyond his home, clothes, furniture, horse, weapons and serving slaves.

cards.title: Who he pays for
cards.ar: يخرج ذلك عن نفسه وعن أولاده الصغار وعن مماليكه ولا يؤدي عن زوجته ولا عن أولاده الكبار وإن كانوا في عياله
cards.en: He pays it for himself, his young children and his slaves. He does not pay it for his wife, or for his grown-up children, even if they live in his household.

cards.ask: Hamza pays the fitra. Who does he pay it for?
source: يخرج ذلك عن نفسه وعن أولاده الصغار وعن مماليكه ولا يؤدي عن زوجته ولا عن أولاده الكبار وإن كانوا في عياله
ولا يخرج عن مكاتبه
cards.why: Himself, young children and serving slaves: yes. His wife, grown children and his mukatab: no.

cards.title: Slaves
cards.ar: والعبد بين شريكين لا فطرة على واحد منهما ويؤدي المولى المسلم الفطرة عن عبده الكافر
cards.en: He does not pay it for his mukatab or for slaves kept for trade. A slave owned by two partners: neither pays for him. A Muslim master pays it for his non-Muslim slave.

cards.ask: Two brothers own one slave together. Who pays his fitra?
cards.source: والعبد بين شريكين لا فطرة على واحد منهما
cards.why: A slave shared between two partners has no fitra on either.

cards.title: How much
cards.ar: والفطرة: نصف صاع من بر أو صاع من تمر أو زبيب أو شعير
cards.en: The fitra is half a sa' (a measure of volume) of wheat, or a full sa' of dates, raisins or barley.

cards.title: The size of a sa'
cards.ar: والصاع عند أبي حنيفه ومحمد ثمانية أرطال بالعراقي وقال أبو يوسف: خمسة أرطال وثلث رطل
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa and Muhammad a sa' is 8 ratls (a ratl is a weight, like a pound) by the Iraqi ratl. Note: Abu Yusuf says 5 and a third ratls.

cards.ask: Hamza pays the fitra in dates for himself and his 2 young daughters. How much?
source: أو صاع من تمر
يخرج ذلك عن نفسه وعن أولاده الصغار
cards.why: A sa' of dates for each of the three people: 3 sa'.

cards.title: When it becomes due
cards.ar: ووجوب الفطرة يتعلق بطلوع الفجر من يوم الفطر فمن مات قبل ذلك لم تجب فطرته ومن أسلم أو ولد بعد طلوع الفجر لم تجب فطرته
cards.en: The fitra becomes due at dawn on the day of Eid al-Fitr. Someone who died before dawn owes none. Someone who became Muslim or was born after dawn owes none.

cards.ask: Aisha's baby is born ten minutes after dawn on Eid morning. Is fitra due for him?
options: No: he was born after dawn
Yes: he was born on Eid day
cards.source: ومن أسلم أو ولد بعد طلوع الفجر لم تجب فطرته
cards.why: The fitra is fixed at dawn. He was born after it, so none is due for him.

cards.title: When to give it
cards.ar: ويستحب للناس أن يخرجوا الفطرة يوم الفطر قبل الخروج إلى المصلى فإن قدموها قبل يوم الفطر جاز وإن أخروها عن يوم الفطر لم تسقط وكان عليهم إخراجها
cards.en: It is mustahabb (recommended) to give it on Eid day before going out to the prayer ground. Giving it before Eid day is allowed. If it is delayed past Eid day it is not dropped: it still has to be given.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Fitra may be paid before Eid day
If delayed past Eid it must still be paid
The fitra is half a sa' of wheat or a sa' of barley
A man pays fitra for his wife
Someone who died the night before Eid owes fitra

source: فإن قدموها قبل يوم الفطر جاز
وإن أخروها عن يوم الفطر لم تسقط
نصف صاع من بر أو صاع من تمر أو زبيب أو شعير
ولا يؤدي عن زوجته
فمن مات قبل ذلك لم تجب فطرته
cards.why: Early payment is allowed, late payment is still owed, and the amounts are right. He does not pay for his wife, and death before dawn means no fitra.

lessons.title: Kinds of fast and the new moon

cards.title: Two kinds
cards.ar: الصوم ضربان: واجب ونفل فالواجب ضربان
cards.en: Fasting is of two kinds: wajib (required) and nafl (extra, voluntary). The wajib kind is itself of two kinds. The first is tied to a set time, like the fast of Ramadan, or a nadhr (a vow) to fast on a named day; its intention may be made in the night before.

cards.title: Fasts owed, and voluntary fasts
cards.ar: والضرب الثاني: ما يثبت في الذمة كقضاء رمضان والنذر المطلق والكفارات فلا يجوز إلا بنية من الليل والنفل كله يجوز بنية قبل الزوال
cards.en: The second wajib kind is a fast you owe, with no set day: qada (making up) of Ramadan, a vow with no named day, and kaffaras (fasts of expiation). These need an intention made in the night. Every voluntary fast is valid with an intention made before zawal (midday).

cards.ask: When must the intention be made?
items: Making up a missed Ramadan day
A vow to fast, with no day named
cards.source: كقضاء رمضان والنذر المطلق والكفارات فلا يجوز إلا بنية من الليل والنفل كله يجوز بنية قبل الزوال
cards.why: Qada, open vows and kaffaras need an intention from the night. Voluntary fasts can be intended before midday.

cards.ask: Amir wakes up, eats nothing, and at 10 in the morning decides to keep a voluntary fast. Is it valid?
options: Yes: a voluntary fast can be intended before midday
No: every fast needs an intention from the night
Only if he fasts the next day too
cards.source: والنفل كله يجوز بنية قبل الزوال
cards.why: 10am is before zawal, and voluntary fasts allow an intention up to then.

cards.title: Looking for the moon
cards.ar: وينبغي للناس أن يلتمسوا الهلال في اليوم التاسع والعشرين من شعبان فإن رأوه صاموا وإن غم عليهم أكملوا عدة شعبان ثلاثين يوما ثم صاموا
cards.en: People should look for the hilal (new crescent moon) on the 29th of Sha'ban. If they see it, they fast. If it is hidden by cloud, they complete Sha'ban as 30 days and then fast.

cards.ask: On the evening of 29 Sha'ban it is cloudy and nobody sees the moon. What happens?
options: Sha'ban is made 30 days, then they fast
They wait for a clear night
cards.source: وإن غم عليهم أكملوا عدة شعبان ثلاثين يوما ثم صاموا
cards.why: When the moon is hidden, Sha'ban is completed as 30 days.

cards.title: One witness
cards.ar: ومن رأى هلال رمضان وحده صام وإن لم يقبل الإمام شهادته وإذا كان بالسماء علة قبل الإمام شهادة الواحد العدل في رؤية الهلال رجلا أو امرأة حرا كان أو عبدا
cards.en: Whoever sees the Ramadan moon by himself fasts, even if the imam does not accept his word. When something in the sky (like cloud or dust) blocks the view, the imam accepts one 'adl (trustworthy) witness: man or woman, free or slave. When the sky is clear, one witness is not enough: a large crowd must see it.

cards.ask: Nadia alone saw the Ramadan moon. The imam did not accept her word. What does she do?
options: She waits for the imam's day
She fasts only if others agree
cards.source: ومن رأى هلال رمضان وحده صام وإن لم يقبل الإمام شهادته
cards.why: She saw it herself, so she fasts, whatever the imam decided.

cards.ask: The sky is clear. One trustworthy man says he saw the Ramadan moon, and nobody else did. Is his word accepted?
options: No: with a clear sky, a large crowd must see it
Yes: one trustworthy witness is enough
Yes, if he swears an oath
cards.source: لم تقبل شهادته حتى يراه جمع كثير يقع العلم بخبرهم
cards.why: One witness is accepted only when the sky is blocked. In a clear sky many must see it.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: A make-up fast needs an intention from the night
A woman's word can count for the Ramadan moon on a cloudy day
If the moon is hidden, Sha'ban becomes 30 days
A voluntary fast needs an intention from the night
Someone who sees the moon alone waits for the imam

source: فلا يجوز إلا بنية من الليل
قبل الإمام شهادة الواحد العدل في رؤية الهلال رجلا أو امرأة
أكملوا عدة شعبان ثلاثين يوما
والنفل كله يجوز بنية قبل الزوال
ومن رأى هلال رمضان وحده صام
cards.why: The first three are right. A voluntary fast can be intended before midday, and whoever sees the moon himself fasts.

cards.title: What fasting is
cards.ar: ووقت الصوم من طلوع الفجر الثاني إلى غروب الشمس
cards.en: The fast lasts from the second (true) dawn until sunset. Fasting means holding back from eating, drinking and intercourse during the day, with an intention.

cards.title: Forgetting
cards.ar: فإن أكل الصائم أو شرب أو جامع ناسيا لم يفطر
cards.en: If a fasting person eats, drinks or has intercourse because he forgot he was fasting, his fast is not broken.

cards.ask: Bilal forgets he is fasting and drinks a glass of water at noon. Then he remembers. What about his fast?
options: It is not broken: he forgot
It is broken: he must make it up
It is broken: make up and kaffara
cards.source: فإن أكل الصائم أو شرب أو جامع ناسيا لم يفطر
cards.why: Eating or drinking out of forgetfulness does not break the fast.

cards.title: Things that do not break it
cards.ar: وإن نام فاحتلم أو نظر إلى امرأة فأنزل أو ادهن أو احتجم أو اكتحل
cards.en: These do not break the fast: a wet dream in sleep, a discharge from looking at a woman, putting oil on the body, cupping (hijama), or putting kohl in the eyes.

cards.title: Kissing
cards.ar: أو قبل لم يفطره فإن أنزل بقبلة أو لمس فعليه القضاء ولا بأس بالقبلة إذا أمن على نفسه ويكره إن لم يأمن
cards.en: A kiss does not break the fast either. But if a kiss or touch leads to a discharge, he must make the day up (qada). Kissing is fine if he trusts himself, and makruh if he does not.

cards.ask: Salim is fasting. He kisses his wife and it leads to a discharge. What does he owe?
options: Nothing: a kiss does not break the fast
He makes up the day and pays kaffara
cards.source: فإن أنزل بقبلة أو لمس فعليه القضاء
cards.why: A kiss alone does not break the fast, but a kiss that leads to a discharge means a make-up day.

cards.title: Vomiting and swallowing stones
cards.ar: وإن ذرعه القيء لم يفطر وإن استقاء عامدا ملء فيه فعليه القضاء ومن ابتلع الحصاة أو الحديد أفطر
cards.en: Vomiting that overcomes you does not break the fast. Making yourself vomit a mouthful on purpose means you make the day up. Swallowing a pebble or a piece of iron breaks the fast.

cards.ask: Does it break the fast?
source: وإن نام فاحتلم
أو احتجم أو اكتحل
وإن ذرعه القيء لم يفطر وإن استقاء عامدا ملء فيه فعليه القضاء ومن ابتلع الحصاة أو الحديد أفطر
cards.why: Sleep, kohl, cupping and unwanted vomiting leave the fast whole. Vomiting on purpose and swallowing a pebble break it.

cards.title: Tasting and chewing
cards.ar: ومن ذاق شيئا بفمه لم يفطر ويكره له ذلك ويكره للمرأة أن تمضغ لصبيها الطعام إذا كان لها منه بد ومضغ العلك لا يفطر الصائم ويكره
cards.en: Tasting something with the mouth does not break the fast, but it is makruh. It is makruh for a woman to chew food for her baby if she has another way. Chewing 'ilk (gum) does not break the fast, but it is makruh.

cards.ask: Maryam is fasting. She chews food to soften it for her baby, though she could mash it instead. What is the ruling?
options: Her fast stands, but it is makruh
cards.source: ويكره للمرأة أن تمضغ لصبيها الطعام إذا كان لها منه بد
cards.why: Chewing does not break the fast, but it is makruh when she has another way.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Chewing gum does not break the fast, but is makruh
A kiss that leads to a discharge means a make-up day
Eating because you forgot does not break the fast
Cupping breaks the fast
Swallowing a piece of iron does not break the fast

source: ومضغ العلك لا يفطر الصائم ويكره
فإن أنزل بقبلة أو لمس فعليه القضاء
فإن أكل الصائم أو شرب أو جامع ناسيا لم يفطر
أو احتجم
ومن ابتلع الحصاة أو الحديد أفطر
cards.why: The first three are right. Cupping does not break the fast, and swallowing iron does.

cards.title: Breaking it on purpose
cards.ar: ومن جامع عامدا في أحد السبيلين أو أكل أو شرب ما يتغذى به أو يتداوى به فعليه القضاء والكفارة مثل كفارة الظهار
cards.en: Whoever has intercourse on purpose, or eats or drinks on purpose something taken as food or as medicine, must make up the day (qada) and also pay the kaffara (expiation). It is the same kaffara as for zihar, which the book explains in its own chapter.

cards.ask: In Ramadan, Tariq eats lunch on purpose. What must he do?
options: Make up the day and pay the kaffara
cards.source: أو أكل أو شرب ما يتغذى به أو يتداوى به فعليه القضاء والكفارة
cards.why: Eating on purpose brings both: the make-up day and the kaffara.

cards.title: When there is no kaffara
cards.ar: ومن جامع فيما دون الفرج فأنزل فعليه القضاء ولا كفارة عليه في إفساد الصوم في غير رمضان كفارة
cards.en: Intimacy short of intercourse that leads to a discharge means making up the day, with no kaffara. And spoiling a fast outside Ramadan has no kaffara.

cards.ask: In Shawwal, Huda is fasting a make-up day for Ramadan, and eats on purpose. Does she owe a kaffara?
options: No: there is no kaffara outside Ramadan
cards.source: في إفساد الصوم في غير رمضان كفارة
cards.why: The kaffara is only for spoiling a Ramadan fast.

cards.title: Things that reach inside
cards.ar: ومن احتقن أو استعط أوقطر في أذنيه أو داوى جائفة أو آمة بدواء فوصل إلى جوفه أو دماغه أفطر
cards.en: These break the fast: an enema, sniffing medicine up the nose, drops in the ears, or medicine on a deep wound of the belly (ja'ifa) or head (amma) that reaches inside the body or the brain.

cards.title: A note
cards.ar: وإن أقطر في إحليله لم يفطر عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف يفطر
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa, drops put into the urethra do not break the fast. Note: Abu Yusuf says they do.

cards.ask: Zaid puts drops in his ears while fasting. What about his fast?
options: It is makruh but not broken
cards.source: أوقطر في أذنيه
cards.why: Ear drops are listed with the things that break the fast.

cards.ask: What is owed?
items: Eating a meal on purpose in Ramadan
Drinking medicine on purpose in Ramadan
A discharge from intimacy short of intercourse
source: ومن جامع عامدا في أحد السبيلين أو أكل أو شرب ما يتغذى به أو يتداوى به فعليه القضاء والكفارة
ومن جامع فيما دون الفرج فأنزل فعليه القضاء ولا كفارة عليه
فإن أنزل بقبلة أو لمس فعليه القضاء
cards.why: Eating, drinking food or medicine, or intercourse, on purpose, bring the kaffara. A discharge without intercourse is made up only.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: An enema breaks the fast
Medicine on a deep head wound that reaches the brain breaks the fast
The fasting kaffara is like the kaffara of zihar
Spoiling a voluntary fast brings a kaffara
Drinking medicine on purpose in Ramadan needs no kaffara

source: ومن احتقن
أو آمة بدواء فوصل إلى جوفه أو دماغه أفطر
مثل كفارة الظهار
في إفساد الصوم في غير رمضان كفارة
أو يتداوى به فعليه القضاء والكفارة
cards.why: The first three are right. There is no kaffara outside Ramadan, and medicine taken on purpose does bring it.

cards.title: The sick and the traveller
cards.ar: ومن كان مريضا في رمضان فخاف إن صام زاد مرضه أفطر وقضى وإن كان مسافرا لا يستضر بالصوم فصومه أفضل وإن أفطر وقضى جاز
cards.en: A sick person who fears fasting will make him worse breaks the fast and makes it up later. A traveller whom fasting does not harm does better to fast; if he breaks it and makes it up, that is allowed.

cards.ask: Ali travels in Ramadan, and fasting does not harm him. What is best?
options: Fasting is better, but breaking it and making up is allowed
He must fast: breaking it is not allowed
cards.source: وإن كان مسافرا لا يستضر بالصوم فصومه أفضل وإن أفطر وقضى جاز
cards.why: For a traveller who is not harmed, fasting is better, and breaking it is still allowed.

cards.title: If they die
cards.ar: وإن مات المريض أو المسافر وهما على حالهما لم يلزمهما القضاء وإن صح المريض أو أقام المسافر ثم ماتا لزمهما القضاء بقدر الصحة والإقامة
cards.en: If the sick person or traveller dies while still sick or travelling, they owe no make-up. If the sick person got better, or the traveller got home, and then died, they owe make-up days for as many days as they were well or at home.

cards.ask: Umar was sick and missed 10 days of Ramadan. After Ramadan he was well for 4 days, then he died. How many make-up days did he owe?
cards.source: لزمهما القضاء بقدر الصحة والإقامة
cards.why: He owes only as many days as he was well: 4.

cards.title: Making up the days
cards.ar: وقضاء رمضان إن شاء فرقه وإن شاء تابعه فإن أخره حتى دخل رمضان آخر صام رمضان الثاني وقضى الأول بعده ولا فدية عليه
cards.en: Make-up days for Ramadan may be split up or kept in a row, as you like. If you put them off until the next Ramadan comes in, you fast that Ramadan and make up the old days after it. There is no fidya (food paid instead) for the delay.

cards.ask: Sana owes 5 days from last Ramadan and has not made them up. The new Ramadan has started. What does she do?
options: Fast this Ramadan, then make up the 5 days, with no fidya
Pay fidya instead of the 5 days
cards.source: صام رمضان الثاني وقضى الأول بعده ولا فدية عليه
cards.why: She fasts the new Ramadan and makes up the old days after it. No fidya.

cards.title: Pregnant and nursing women
cards.ar: إذا خافتا على ولديهما أفطرتا وقضتا ولا فدية عليهما
cards.en: A pregnant woman, and a nursing mother, who fear for their child, break the fast and make it up later. They owe no fidya.

cards.title: The very old
cards.ar: والشيخ الفاني الذي لا يقدر على الصيام يفطر ويطعم لكل يوم مسكينا كما يطعم في الكفارات
cards.en: A very old man who cannot fast does not fast. For each day he feeds a miskin (a needy person), as is done in kaffaras.

cards.ask: Grandpa Yusuf is 90 and cannot fast at all. What does he do in Ramadan?
options: He does not fast, and feeds a miskin for each day
He fasts as much as he can
cards.source: والشيخ الفاني الذي لا يقدر على الصيام يفطر ويطعم لكل يوم مسكينا
cards.why: He breaks the fast and feeds a needy person for every day.

cards.title: Someone who dies owing days
cards.ar: ومن مات وعليه قضاء رمضان فأوصى به أطعم عنه وليه لكل يوم مسكينا نصف صاع من بر أو صاعا من تمر أو صاعا من شعير
cards.en: If someone dies owing Ramadan days and left a wasiyya (an instruction in his will) about it, his wali (guardian, the next of kin in charge) feeds one miskin for each day: half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates or of barley.

cards.ask: Ahmad dies owing 3 days of Ramadan, and his will asks for them to be paid. What does his wali do?
options: Feed 3 miskins: half a sa' of wheat each
Feed 1 miskin half a sa' of wheat
cards.source: أطعم عنه وليه لكل يوم مسكينا نصف صاع من بر
cards.why: One miskin for each day: 3 miskins, each given half a sa' of wheat (or a sa' of dates or barley).

cards.ask: Make up later, or feed instead?
items: A sick man who fears getting worse
A traveller who broke the fast
A pregnant woman who fears for her baby
A very old man who cannot fast
A nursing mother who fears for her child
source: أفطر وقضى
وإن أفطر وقضى جاز
أفطرتا وقضتا ولا فدية عليهما
يفطر ويطعم لكل يوم مسكينا
cards.why: The sick, the traveller and the two women make up the days. Only the very old man feeds instead.

cards.title: Breaking a voluntary fast
cards.ar: ومن دخل في صوم التطوع أو صلاة التطوع ثم أفسده قضاه
cards.en: If someone starts a tatawwu' (voluntary) fast or prayer and then spoils it, he must make it up.

cards.ask: Rania starts a voluntary Monday fast, then eats at noon. What now?
options: She must make it up and pay kaffara
cards.source: ومن دخل في صوم التطوع أو صلاة التطوع ثم أفسده قضاه
cards.why: A voluntary fast that is started and spoiled must be made up.

cards.title: Coming of age, becoming Muslim
cards.ar: وإذا بلغ الصبي أو أسلم الكافر في رمضان أمسكا بقية يومهما وصاما ما بعده ولم يقضيا ما مضى
cards.en: If a boy comes of age, or a non-Muslim becomes Muslim, during Ramadan, they hold back from food for the rest of that day, fast the days after, and do not make up the days that went before.

cards.ask: John becomes Muslim at noon on the 15th of Ramadan. What does he do?
options: Hold back the rest of the day, fast from then on, make up nothing
Make up days 1 to 15 after Ramadan
cards.source: أمسكا بقية يومهما وصاما ما بعده ولم يقضيا ما مضى
cards.why: He holds back for the rest of that day and fasts after it. The days before he became Muslim are not made up.

cards.title: Fainting and madness
cards.ar: ومن أغمي عليه في رمضان لم يقض اليوم الذي حدث فيه الإغماء وقضى ما بعده وإذا أفاق المجنون في بعض رمضان قضى ما مضى منه
cards.en: Someone who faints in Ramadan does not make up the day the fainting began, but makes up the days after it. A madman who becomes sane during part of Ramadan makes up the days of it that passed.

cards.ask: Hasan faints on the 10th of Ramadan and is unconscious on the 10th, 11th and 12th. Which days does he make up?
cards.source: لم يقض اليوم الذي حدث فيه الإغماء وقضى ما بعده
cards.why: The day the fainting began is not made up. The days after it are.

cards.title: Periods and coming home
cards.ar: وإذا حاضت المرأة أفطرت وقضت
cards.en: A woman whose period (hayd) comes does not fast, and makes up the days later. If a traveller comes home, or a woman's period ends, during the day, they hold back from food and drink for the rest of that day.

cards.ask: Aisha's period ends at 11 in the morning in Ramadan. What does she do for the rest of that day?
options: Hold back from food and drink until sunset
Eat normally: the day is already lost
Start a fast that counts for that day
cards.source: أو طهرت الحائض في بعض النهار أمسكا عن الطعام والشراب بقية يومهما
cards.why: She holds back for the rest of the day out of respect for Ramadan, and makes the day up later.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: A spoiled voluntary prayer must be made up
A madman who recovers mid-Ramadan makes up the days that passed
A woman on her period does not fast and makes up later
A new Muslim makes up the earlier days of Ramadan
A traveller who comes home at noon may eat freely

source: أو صلاة التطوع ثم أفسده قضاه
وإذا أفاق المجنون في بعض رمضان قضى ما مضى منه
وإذا حاضت المرأة أفطرت وقضت
ولم يقضيا ما مضى
أمسكا عن الطعام والشراب بقية يومهما
cards.why: The first three are right. A new Muslim does not make up past days, and a traveller who arrives holds back for the rest of the day.

lessons.title: Mistakes about the time, and the Eid moon

cards.title: Getting the time wrong
cards.ar: ومن تسحر وهو يظن أن الفجر لم يطلع أو أفطر وهو يرى أن الشمس قد غربت ثم تبين أن الفجر كان قد طلع أو أن الشمس لم تغرب قضى ذلك اليوم ولا كفارة عليه
cards.en: Someone who eats suhur (the meal before dawn) thinking dawn has not come, or breaks his fast thinking the sun has set, and then finds out dawn had come or the sun had not set, makes up that day. He owes no kaffara.

cards.ask: Ibrahim breaks his fast thinking the sun has set. Then he sees it has not. What does he owe?
options: Make up the day, with no kaffara
Make up the day and pay kaffara
cards.source: قضى ذلك اليوم ولا كفارة عليه
cards.why: A mistake about the time means a make-up day, but no kaffara.

cards.ask: Complete it: what does the one who ate after dawn by mistake do?
cards.ar: أو أن الشمس لم تغرب ____ ولا كفارة عليه
cards.source: أو أن الشمس لم تغرب قضى ذلك اليوم ولا كفارة عليه
cards.why: قضى ذلك اليوم: he makes up that day.

cards.ask: Omar eats suhur thinking it is still night. Later he learns dawn had already come. What does he owe?
options: He makes up the day, with no kaffara
He makes up the day and pays kaffara
cards.source: ومن تسحر وهو يظن أن الفجر لم يطلع
cards.why: He ate after dawn without knowing, so he makes up the day, without kaffara.

cards.title: The Eid moon
cards.ar: ومن رأى هلال الفطر وحده لم يفطر وإذا كان بالسماء علة لم تقبل في هلال الفطر إلا شهادة رجلين أو رجل وامرأتين وإن لم يكن بالسماء علة لم تقبل إلا شهادة جمع كثير
cards.en: Whoever sees the Eid moon by himself does not break his fast (he keeps fasting with everyone). When something in the sky blocks the view, only the witness of two men, or a man and two women, is accepted for the Eid moon. When the sky is clear, only a large crowd is accepted.

cards.ask: Yahya alone sees the Eid moon on the 29th night. Nobody else does. What does he do the next day?
options: He fasts only half the day
cards.source: ومن رأى هلال الفطر وحده لم يفطر
cards.why: For the Eid moon, one who sees it alone does not break his fast.

cards.ask: It is cloudy on the 29th of Ramadan. One man and two women say they saw the Eid moon. Is their word accepted?
options: No: it must be two men
No: a large crowd is needed
cards.source: لم تقبل في هلال الفطر إلا شهادة رجلين أو رجل وامرأتين
cards.why: With a blocked sky, a man and two women are enough for the Eid moon.

cards.ask: Which moon is it? (the sky is cloudy)
items: Needs two men, or a man and two women
Seeing it alone means you fast
Seeing it alone does not let you stop fasting
source: قبل الإمام شهادة الواحد العدل في رؤية الهلال
لم تقبل في هلال الفطر إلا شهادة رجلين أو رجل وامرأتين
ومن رأى هلال رمضان وحده صام
ومن رأى هلال الفطر وحده لم يفطر
cards.why: The Ramadan moon needs one witness on a cloudy day, and seeing it alone means you fast. The Eid moon needs more witnesses, and seeing it alone does not end your fast.

cards.title: What i'tikaf is
cards.ar: الاعتكاف مستحب وهو اللبث في المسجد مع الصوم ونية الاعتكاف
cards.en: I'tikaf is mustahabb (recommended). It is staying in the masjid, while fasting, with the intention of i'tikaf.

cards.ask: What does i'tikaf need?

options.text: Staying in the masjid
Fasting
The intention of i'tikaf
Staying at home
Keeping silent

source: وهو اللبث في المسجد مع الصوم ونية الاعتكاف
ويكره له الصمت
cards.why: The masjid, fasting and the intention. Silence is actually makruh.

cards.title: What is forbidden
cards.ar: ويحرم على المعتكف: الوط واللمس والقبلة
cards.en: For the mu'takif (the one in i'tikaf), intercourse, touching and kissing are haram.

cards.title: Leaving the masjid
cards.ar: ولا يخرج من المسجد إلا لحاجة الإنسان أو الجمعة ولا بأس بأن يبيع ويبتاع في المسجد من غير أن يحضر السلع
cards.en: He leaves the masjid only for a person's needs (like the toilet) or for Jumu'a. He may buy and sell in the masjid, as long as he does not bring the goods in.

cards.ask: During i'tikaf: allowed or not?
items: Agreeing a sale without bringing the goods in
Bringing goods into the masjid to sell
Going out to visit a friend
source: ولا يخرج من المسجد إلا لحاجة الإنسان أو الجمعة
ولا بأس بأن يبيع ويبتاع في المسجد من غير أن يحضر السلع
ويحرم على المعتكف: الوط واللمس والقبلة
cards.why: Needs, Jumu'a and a sale without the goods are fine. Goods in the masjid, kissing and other outings are not.

cards.ask: Yusuf is in i'tikaf. He agrees to sell his sheep to a man in the masjid; the sheep stay on his farm. Is that allowed?
options: Yes: the goods are not brought in
No: no selling at all in i'tikaf
cards.source: ولا بأس بأن يبيع ويبتاع في المسجد من غير أن يحضر السلع
cards.why: Buying and selling is fine as long as the goods are not brought into the masjid.

cards.title: Speech, and what ruins it
cards.ar: إلا بخير ويكره له الصمت فإن جامع المعتكف ليلا أو نهارا بطل اعتكافه
cards.en: He speaks only good, and keeping silent is makruh for him. If he has intercourse, by night or by day, his i'tikaf is ruined.

cards.ask: Hamid is in i'tikaf. At night (when he is not fasting) he has intercourse with his wife. What happens?
cards.source: فإن جامع المعتكف ليلا أو نهارا بطل اعتكافه
cards.why: By night or by day, intercourse ruins the i'tikaf.

cards.title: Vowing days
cards.ar: ومن أوجب على نفسه اعتكاف أيام لزمه اعتكافها بلياليها وكانت متتابعة وإن لم يشترط التتابع
cards.en: If someone vows to make i'tikaf for some days, he must do them with their nights, one after another in a row, even if he did not say "in a row".

cards.ask: Imran vows 3 days of i'tikaf and says nothing about doing them in a row. What must he do?
options: 3 days with their nights, in a row
cards.source: لزمه اعتكافها بلياليها وكانت متتابعة وإن لم يشترط التتابع
cards.why: Vowed days come with their nights and in a row, even if he did not say so.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: I'tikaf needs fasting
Silence is makruh in i'tikaf
He may go out for Jumu'a
Intercourse at night does not ruin it
Vowed days need not be in a row

source: مع الصوم ونية الاعتكاف
ويكره له الصمت
إلا لحاجة الإنسان أو الجمعة
فإن جامع المعتكف ليلا أو نهارا بطل اعتكافه
وكانت متتابعة وإن لم يشترط التتابع
cards.why: Fasting, the dislike of silence and going out for Jumu'a are right. Intercourse ruins it by night too, and vowed days go in a row.

cards.title: Who Hajj is for
cards.ar: الحج: واجب على الأحرار البالغين العقلاء الأصحاء
cards.en: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah. It is a duty on every Muslim who is free (not a slave), baligh (has reached adulthood), sane, and healthy in body.

cards.ask: Which of these are conditions for Hajj being a duty on someone?

options.text: Being free
Having reached adulthood
Being sane
Being healthy
Having already done an umrah
Living close to Makkah

cards.source: الحج: واجب على الأحرار البالغين العقلاء الأصحاء
cards.why: The four named are: free, adult, sane, healthy. An earlier umrah and living nearby are not among them.

cards.title: Being able to afford it
cards.ar: إذا قدروا على الزاد والراحلة فاضلا عن مسكنه وما لا بد منه وعن نفقة عياله إلى حين عوده وكان الطريق آمنا
cards.en: It is a duty only when he can pay for provisions (food for the journey) and a ride, using money left over after his home, the things he cannot do without, and his family's living costs until he comes back. And the road must be safe.

cards.ask: Yusuf has just enough money for the journey and his ride. But if he spends it, his wife and children will have nothing to live on while he is away. Is Hajj a duty on him now?
options: No: his family's costs until he returns come first
Yes: he has the fare and the ride
Yes, but he must go by the cheapest ride
cards.source: وعن نفقة عياله إلى حين عوده
cards.why: The money for the journey must be extra to what his family needs until he is back. His isn't, so Hajj is not yet a duty on him.

cards.ask: Ahmad is healthy and has plenty of money, but the only road to Makkah this year is unsafe because of war. Must he go?
options: No: the road must be safe
Yes: he has the money, so he must go
Yes, if he takes a guard
cards.source: وكان الطريق آمنا
cards.why: One condition is that the road is safe. While it is not, Hajj is not yet a duty for him.

cards.title: A woman's mahram
cards.ar: ويعتبر في المرأة أن يكون لها محرم يحج بها أو زوج ولا يجوز لها أن تحج بغيرهما إذا كان بينها وبين مكة مسيرة ثلاثة أيام ولياليها
cards.en: A woman also needs a mahram (a close male relative she can never marry, like her father, son or brother) or her husband to travel with her. She may not go without one of them if Makkah is three days and nights of travel away or more.

cards.ask: Complete it: how far away does a woman need a mahram or husband?
cards.ar: ولا يجوز لها أن تحج بغيرهما إذا كان بينها وبين مكة مسيرة ____ أيام ولياليها
cards.source: ولا يجوز لها أن تحج بغيرهما إذا كان بينها وبين مكة مسيرة ثلاثة أيام ولياليها
cards.why: Three days and nights of travel. From that distance she needs a mahram or her husband with her.

cards.title: A boy or a slave in ihram
cards.ar: وإذا بلغ الصبي بعد ما أحرم أو أعتق العبد فمضيا على ذلك لم يجزيهما عن حجة الإسلام
cards.en: Ihram is the sacred state a pilgrim enters for Hajj. If a boy enters ihram and then reaches adulthood, or a slave enters it and is then set free, and they simply carry on, that Hajj does not count as their "Hajj of Islam" (the one Hajj every Muslim owes).

cards.ask: Zayd enters ihram at 14 and reaches adulthood during the days of Hajj. He carries on in the same ihram and finishes. Has he done his Hajj of Islam?
options: No: it does not count as his Hajj of Islam
Yes: he was an adult before it finished
Yes, if he was an adult before Arafa
cards.source: وإذا بلغ الصبي بعد ما أحرم أو أعتق العبد فمضيا على ذلك لم يجزيهما عن حجة الإسلام
cards.why: He entered ihram as a child and just carried on, so it does not count as his obligatory Hajj.

cards.ask: Is Hajj a duty on them now?
items: A free, healthy adult with money to spare and a safe road
A man whose family would have nothing while he is away
A woman far from Makkah with no mahram or husband to go with her
A child who is not yet an adult
A wealthy, sane, healthy adult whose road is safe
source: الحج: واجب على الأحرار البالغين العقلاء الأصحاء إذا قدروا على الزاد والراحلة
ويعتبر في المرأة أن يكون لها محرم يحج بها أو زوج
cards.why: It is a duty on the free, adult, sane and healthy who can afford it with money to spare and a safe road. A woman also needs a mahram or husband.

cards.title: The miqats of Madinah, Iraq and Syria
cards.ar: والمواقيت التي لا يجوز أن يتجاوزها الإنسان إلا محرما: لأهل المدينة ذو الحليفة ولأهل العراق ذات عرق ولأهل الشام الجحفة
cards.en: A miqat is a fixed place on the way to Makkah. A pilgrim may not pass it without being in ihram. For the people of Madinah it is Dhul-Hulayfa, for Iraq it is Dhat 'Irq, and for Syria (al-Sham) it is al-Juhfa.

cards.title: The miqats of Najd and Yemen
cards.ar: ولأهل نجد قرن المنازل ولأهل اليمن يلملم
cards.en: For the people of Najd it is Qarn al-Manazil, and for Yemen it is Yalamlam.

cards.ask: Bilal sets off for Hajj from Madinah. Where must he be in ihram by?
source: باب تحديد المواقيت
لأهل المدينة ذو الحليفة
cards.why: Dhul-Hulayfa is the miqat for the people of Madinah. Dhat 'Irq is for Iraq and Yalamlam for Yemen.

cards.ask: Which miqat completes it?
cards.ar: ولأهل اليمن ____
cards.source: ولأهل اليمن يلملم
cards.why: Yalamlam is the miqat of Yemen. Al-Juhfa is for Syria and Dhat 'Irq for Iraq.

cards.title: Entering ihram before the miqat
cards.ar: فإن قدم الإحرام على هذه المواقيت جاز
cards.en: If he enters ihram before reaching these miqats, that is allowed.

cards.ask: Hamza, travelling from Syria, puts on ihram at home, days before reaching al-Juhfa. What is the ruling?
options: Not allowed: he must wait for the miqat
Allowed only if he redoes it at al-Juhfa
cards.source: فإن قدم الإحرام على هذه المواقيت جاز
cards.why: Entering ihram before the miqat is allowed. Only passing the miqat without ihram is not.

cards.title: Those who live inside the miqats
cards.ar: ومن كان منزله بعد المواقيت فميقاته الحل ومن كان بمكة فميقاته في الحج الحرم وفي العمرة الحل
cards.en: The Haram is the sacred area around Makkah. The Hill is the land outside the Haram. Someone who lives inside the miqats (closer to Makkah) enters ihram in the Hill. Someone in Makkah enters ihram for Hajj in the Haram, but for umrah (the lesser pilgrimage) he goes out to the Hill.

cards.ask: Khadija lives in Makkah and wants to do an umrah. Where does she enter ihram?
options: In the Hill, outside the Haram
In the Haram, at her home
cards.source: ومن كان بمكة فميقاته في الحج الحرم وفي العمرة الحل
cards.why: For umrah, someone in Makkah enters ihram in the Hill. Only for Hajj is the Haram her miqat.

cards.ask: Where does each one enter ihram?
items: A man living in Makkah, for Hajj
A woman living in Makkah, for umrah
Someone living between the miqat and Makkah
cards.source: ومن كان منزله بعد المواقيت فميقاته الحل ومن كان بمكة فميقاته في الحج الحرم وفي العمرة الحل
cards.why: Only someone in Makkah doing Hajj enters ihram in the Haram. For umrah, and for those inside the miqats, it is the Hill.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Al-Juhfa is the miqat of Syria
Qarn al-Manazil is the miqat of Najd
Entering ihram before the miqat is allowed
Dhat 'Irq is the miqat of Madinah
One may pass the miqat without ihram and enter it in Makkah

source: ولأهل الشام الجحفة
ولأهل نجد قرن المنازل
فإن قدم الإحرام على هذه المواقيت جاز
لأهل المدينة ذو الحليفة ولأهل العراق ذات عرق
والمواقيت التي لا يجوز أن يتجاوزها الإنسان إلا محرما
cards.why: Al-Juhfa is Syria's, Qarn al-Manazil is Najd's, and early ihram is allowed. Dhat 'Irq is Iraq's, and the miqat may not be passed without ihram.

cards.title: Washing and the two cloths
cards.ar: وإذا أراد الإحرام اغتسل أو توضأ - والغسل أفضل - ولبس ثوبين جديدين أو غسيلين إزارا ورداء
cards.en: When he wants to enter ihram he takes a ghusl (full bath) or makes wudu, and ghusl is better. He puts on two cloths, new or washed: an izar (a sheet wrapped round the waist) and a rida' (a sheet over the shoulders).

cards.ask: Umar is at the miqat and only has time for wudu, not a full ghusl. Can he enter ihram?
options: Yes: wudu is enough, though ghusl is better
cards.source: اغتسل أو توضأ - والغسل أفضل -
cards.why: Either ghusl or wudu is fine. Ghusl is only the better of the two.

cards.title: Perfume, two rak'as and the du'a
cards.ar: ومس طيبا إن كان له طيب وصلى ركعتين وقال: اللهم إني أريد الحج فيسره لي وتقبله مني
cards.en: He puts on perfume if he has any, prays two rak'as, and says: "O Allah, I want to do Hajj, so make it easy for me and accept it from me."

cards.title: The talbiya
cards.ar: ثم يلبي عقيب صلاته فإن كان مفردا بالحج نوى بتلبيته الحج
cards.en: Then, right after his prayer, he says the talbiya. If he is a mufrid (doing Hajj alone, with no umrah joined to it), he intends Hajj with his talbiya.

cards.ask: Put the steps of entering ihram in order.
steps: Take a ghusl or make wudu
Put on the izar and rida'
Say the du'a: "O Allah, I want to do Hajj..."
source: وإذا أراد الإحرام اغتسل أو توضأ
ولبس ثوبين جديدين أو غسيلين إزارا ورداء
وصلى ركعتين وقال: اللهم إني أريد الحج
ثم يلبي عقيب صلاته
cards.why: He washes, dresses in the two cloths, prays two rak'as and makes the du'a, and then, after his prayer, says the talbiya.

cards.title: The words of the talbiya
cards.ar: والتلبية أن يقول: لبيك اللهم لبيك لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك لا شريك لك ولا ينبغي أن يخل بشي من هذه الكلمات فإن زاد فيها جاز
cards.en: The talbiya is: "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk..." (Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. All praise and blessing are Yours, and the kingdom. You have no partner.) He should not leave out any of these words. If he adds more, that is allowed.

cards.ask: Complete the talbiya.
cards.ar: لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد ____ لك والملك
cards.source: لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك
cards.why: "Inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk": all praise and blessing are Yours, and the kingdom.

cards.ask: Ali says the full talbiya and then adds some more words of praise of his own. What is the ruling?
options: Allowed, as long as he leaves nothing out
Not allowed: no words may be added
cards.source: ولا ينبغي أن يخل بشي من هذه الكلمات فإن زاد فيها جاز
cards.why: Adding is allowed. What he should not do is leave out any of the set words.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Ghusl is better than wudu before ihram
The two cloths may be new or washed
The talbiya comes right after the two rak'as
Perfume is forbidden before ihram
A word of the talbiya may be dropped if one adds another

source: والغسل أفضل
ولبس ثوبين جديدين أو غسيلين
ثم يلبي عقيب صلاته
ومس طيبا إن كان له طيب
ولا ينبغي أن يخل بشي من هذه الكلمات
cards.why: Ghusl is better, the cloths may be new or washed, and the talbiya follows the prayer. Perfume before ihram is fine, and no word should be dropped.

cards.title: Ihram begins with the talbiya
cards.ar: فإذا لبى فقد أحرم فليتق ما نهى الله عنه من الرفث والفسوق والجدال ولا يقتل صيدا ولا يشير إليه ولا يدل عليه
cards.en: Once he says the talbiya, he is a muhrim (in ihram). He must keep away from what Allah forbade: rafath (intimate talk and relations), fusuq (sins) and jidal (quarrelling). He may not kill a wild animal (game), point at one, or show anyone where it is.

cards.ask: Sa'd is in ihram. He sees a deer and points it out to a friend who is hunting. Is that allowed?
options: No: he may not even point at game
Yes, since he did not kill it
Yes, if his friend is not in ihram
cards.source: ولا يقتل صيدا ولا يشير إليه ولا يدل عليه
cards.why: A muhrim may not kill game, point at it, or show where it is.

cards.title: Clothes he may not wear
cards.ar: ولا يلبس قميصا ولا سراويل ولا عمامة ولا قلنسوة ولا قباء ولا خفين إلا أن لا يجد النعلين فيقطعهما أسفل الكعبين
cards.en: He does not wear a shirt, trousers, a turban, a cap or a qaba' (a long coat). Nor khuffs (leather socks), unless he cannot find sandals: then he cuts the khuffs down so they sit below the ankle bones.

cards.ask: Hasan is in ihram and cannot find any sandals, only khuffs. What does he do?
options: Cut them down below the ankle bones and wear them
Go barefoot: khuffs are never allowed
cards.source: ولا خفين إلا أن لا يجد النعلين فيقطعهما أسفل الكعبين
cards.why: Without sandals he may wear khuffs, once they are cut down below the ankle bones.

cards.title: Head, face, perfume, hair and nails
cards.ar: ولا يغطي رأسه ولا وجهه ولا يمس طيبا ولا يحلق رأسه ولا شعر بدنه ولا يقص من لحيته ولا من ظفره
cards.en: He does not cover his head or face, touch perfume, shave his head or body hair, or trim his beard or nails.

cards.title: Dyed cloth
cards.ar: ولا يلبس ثوبا مصبوغا بورس زعفران ولا عصفر إلا أن يكون غسلا لا ينفض
cards.en: He does not wear cloth dyed with wars (a yellow, scented plant dye), saffron or safflower, unless it has been washed so much that the colour no longer comes off.

cards.title: What he may do
cards.ar: ولا بأس أن يغتسل ويدخل الحمام ويستظل بالبيت والمخمل ويشد في وسطه الهميان
cards.en: There is no harm in him taking a bath, going into a bathhouse, sitting in the shade of a building or a covered litter, or tying a himyan (money belt) round his waist.

cards.title: Khitmi, and saying the talbiya often
cards.ar: ولا يغتسل رأسه ولا لحيته بالخطمي ويكثر من التلبية عقب الصلوات وكلما علا شرفا أو هبط واديا أو لقي ركبانا وبالأسحار
cards.en: He does not wash his head or beard with khitmi (a scented plant wash). He says the talbiya often: after prayers, each time he climbs a rise or goes down into a valley, when he meets riders, and before dawn.

cards.ask: Allowed for a man in ihram, or not?
items: Sitting in the shade of a building
Tying a money belt round his waist
source: ولا بأس أن يغتسل ويدخل الحمام ويستظل بالبيت والمخمل ويشد في وسطه الهميان
ولا قلنسوة
ولا يقص من لحيته
ولا يغتسل رأسه ولا لحيته بالخطمي
cards.why: A bath, shade and a money belt are fine. A cap, trimming the beard and khitmi are not.

cards.ask: Uthman, in ihram, finds the sun too hot and sits in the shade of a building. What is the ruling?
options: Forbidden: it is like covering the head
cards.source: ويستظل بالبيت والمخمل
cards.why: Sitting in the shade of a building or litter is allowed. Only covering the head itself is forbidden.

cards.ask: When does he say the talbiya a lot?

options.text: After the prayers
When he climbs a rise
When he meets riders
Before dawn
Only once, at the miqat

cards.source: ويكثر من التلبية عقب الصلوات وكلما علا شرفا أو هبط واديا أو لقي ركبانا وبالأسحار
cards.why: He says it often: after prayers, on rises and in valleys, on meeting riders, and before dawn. It is not only once.

cards.ask: Which of these are forbidden in ihram?

options.text: Quarrelling
Covering the face
Wearing cloth dyed with saffron that still runs
Going into a bathhouse
Wearing an izar and rida'

source: من الرفث والفسوق والجدال
ولا يغطي رأسه ولا وجهه
ولا يلبس ثوبا مصبوغا بورس زعفران
ولا بأس أن يغتسل ويدخل الحمام
cards.why: Quarrelling, covering the face and dyed cloth are forbidden. A bathhouse is fine, and the izar and rida' are the ihram clothes.

cards.title: Going first to the Masjid
cards.ar: فإذا دخل مكة ابتدأ بالمسجد الحرام فإذا عاين البيت كبر وهلل ثم ابتدأ بالحجر الأسود فاستقبله وكبر ورفع يديه واستلمه وقبله إن استطاع من غير أن يؤدي مسلما
cards.en: On entering Makkah he goes first to al-Masjid al-Haram. When he sees the House (the Ka'ba) he says "Allahu akbar" and "La ilaha illa Allah". Then he starts at the Black Stone: faces it, says takbir, raises his hands, and touches and kisses it if he can, without hurting any Muslim.

cards.ask: Hamid can only reach the Black Stone by pushing people out of the way. What should he do?
options: Not push: he touches it only if he can without hurting anyone
Push through: kissing it is required
Leave the tawaf until the crowd is gone
cards.source: واستلمه وقبله إن استطاع من غير أن يؤدي مسلما
cards.why: He touches and kisses it only if he can do so without harming a Muslim.

cards.title: Seven circuits
cards.ar: ثم آخذ عن يمينه مما يلي الباب وقد اضطبع رداءه قبل ذلك فيطوف بالبيت سبعة أشواط
cards.en: Then he goes to his right, towards the door, and walks round the House seven shawts (circuits). Before that he does idtiba': he puts his rida' under his right arm and over his left shoulder.

cards.title: Behind the Hatim, and ramal
cards.ar: ويجعل طوافه من وراء الحطيم ويرمل في الأشواط الثلاثة الأول ويمشي فيما بقي على هينته ويستلم الحجر كلما مر به إن استطاع ويختم الطواف بالاستلام
cards.en: He goes round outside the Hatim (the low curved wall beside the Ka'ba). He does ramal (walks quickly with short steps, moving his shoulders) in the first three circuits, and walks normally in the rest. He touches the Stone each time he passes it if he can, and ends the tawaf by touching it.

cards.ask: In which circuits does he do ramal?
cards.source: ويرمل في الأشواط الثلاثة الأول ويمشي فيما بقي على هينته
cards.why: Ramal is in the first three circuits. In the other four he walks at his normal pace.

cards.title: Two rak'as at the Maqam
cards.ar: ثم يأتي المقام فيصلي عنده ركعتين أو حيث تيسر من المسجد
cards.en: Then he goes to the Maqam (the Station of Ibrahim) and prays two rak'as there, or wherever in the Masjid is easy.

cards.ask: Put the arrival rites in order.
steps: Say takbir and tahlil on seeing the House
Face the Black Stone and touch it
Go to the right and walk seven circuits
Pray two rak'as at the Maqam
source: فإذا دخل مكة ابتدأ بالمسجد الحرام فإذا عاين البيت كبر وهلل ثم ابتدأ بالحجر الأسود
ثم آخذ عن يمينه
ثم يأتي المقام فيصلي عنده ركعتين
cards.why: Masjid, takbir on seeing the House, the Black Stone, seven circuits, then two rak'as at the Maqam.

cards.title: This is tawaf al-qudum
cards.ar: وهذا الطواف طواف القدوم وهو سنة وليس بواجب وليس على أهل مكة طواف القدوم
cards.en: This is tawaf al-qudum, the tawaf of arrival. It is sunnah, not wajib (required). The people of Makkah have no tawaf al-qudum.

cards.ask: Bilal lives in Makkah and is doing Hajj. Does he do tawaf al-qudum?
options: No: the people of Makkah have none
Yes: it is wajib on everyone
cards.source: وليس على أهل مكة طواف القدوم
cards.why: Tawaf al-qudum is for those arriving. The people of Makkah have no tawaf al-qudum.

cards.ask: The Maqam is packed, so Musa prays his two rak'as after the tawaf at the back of the Masjid. Is that fine?
options: Yes: anywhere in the Masjid that is easy
No: they must be at the Maqam
No: he must wait until it is empty
cards.source: ثم يأتي المقام فيصلي عنده ركعتين أو حيث تيسر من المسجد
cards.why: He prays them at the Maqam, or wherever in the Masjid is easy.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: He walks round outside the Hatim
He ends the tawaf by touching the Stone
Tawaf al-qudum is sunnah
He goes to his left from the Stone
Tawaf al-qudum has five circuits

source: ويجعل طوافه من وراء الحطيم
ويختم الطواف بالاستلام
وهو سنة وليس بواجب
ثم آخذ عن يمينه مما يلي الباب
فيطوف بالبيت سبعة أشواط
cards.why: Outside the Hatim, ending with the Stone, and it is sunnah. He goes to his right, and it is seven circuits.

cards.title: On Safa
cards.ar: ثم يخرج إلى الصفا فيصعد عليه ويستقبل البيت ويكبر ويهلل ويصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدعو الله تعالى بحاجته
cards.en: Then he goes out to Safa (a small hill near the Ka'ba) and climbs it. He faces the House, says takbir and tahlil, sends blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, and asks Allah for what he needs.

cards.title: Walking to Marwa
cards.ar: ثم ينحط نحو المروة ويمشي على هينته فإذا بلغ إلى بطن الوادي سعى بين الميلين الأخضرين سعيا حتى يأتي المروة
cards.en: Then he goes down towards Marwa (the other hill), walking at his normal pace. When he reaches the bottom of the valley, he runs between the two green markers, and then carries on to Marwa.

cards.ask: Sa'd is walking from Safa to Marwa. Where does he run?
cards.source: فإذا بلغ إلى بطن الوادي سعى بين الميلين الأخضرين سعيا
cards.why: He walks normally, and runs only in the valley bottom between the two green markers.

cards.title: On Marwa, and seven rounds
cards.ar: فيصعد عليها ويفعل كما فعل على الصفا وهذا شوط فيطوف سبعة أشواط يبدأ بالصفا ويختم بالمروة
cards.en: He climbs Marwa and does what he did on Safa. That is one shawt (round). He does seven rounds, starting at Safa and ending at Marwa.

cards.ask: Put one round of sa'y in order.
steps: Climb Safa and face the House
Say takbir, tahlil and blessings, and make du'a
Run between the two green markers
Climb Marwa and do as on Safa
source: ثم يخرج إلى الصفا فيصعد عليه ويستقبل البيت
ثم ينحط نحو المروة ويمشي على هينته
سعى بين الميلين الأخضرين
فيصعد عليها ويفعل كما فعل على الصفا
cards.why: Safa first, with its dhikr and du'a, then down towards Marwa, running between the markers, and up Marwa.

cards.ask: Where does sa'y begin? Complete it.
cards.ar: يبدأ ____ ويختم بالمروة
cards.source: يبدأ بالصفا ويختم بالمروة
cards.why: It begins at Safa and ends at Marwa.

cards.ask: Umar has done six rounds of sa'y. Where is he standing, and what is left?
options: At Safa, with one round to Marwa left
At Marwa, and he is finished
At Safa, with two rounds left
source: وهذا شوط فيطوف سبعة أشواط يبدأ بالصفا ويختم بالمروة
cards.why: Each trip from one hill to the other is one round. Six rounds from Safa end at Safa, so one round to Marwa remains, ending at Marwa.

cards.title: Staying in Makkah in ihram
cards.ar: ثم يقيم بمكة حراما يطوف بالبيت كلما بدا له
cards.en: Then he stays in Makkah, still in ihram, and does tawaf round the House whenever he likes.

cards.ask: After sa'y, Ibrahim waits in Makkah, still in ihram, for the days of Hajj. May he do more tawafs?
options: No: no tawaf until the Day of Sacrifice
cards.source: ثم يقيم بمكة حراما يطوف بالبيت كلما بدا له
cards.why: He stays in ihram and does tawaf as often as he wishes.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Sa'y has seven rounds
He faces the House on Safa
He walks normally outside the green markers
He ends sa'y at Safa
He leaves ihram straight after sa'y

source: فيطوف سبعة أشواط يبدأ بالصفا ويختم بالمروة
فيصعد عليه ويستقبل البيت
ويمشي على هينته
ثم يقيم بمكة حراما
cards.why: Seven rounds, facing the House on Safa, walking normally except between the markers. It ends at Marwa, and he stays in ihram.

cards.title: The sermon before Tarwiya
cards.ar: فإذا كان قبل يوم التروية بيوم خطب الإمام خطبة يعلم الناس فيها الخروج إلى منى والصلاة بعرفات والوقوف والإفاضة
cards.en: The Day of Tarwiya is the day before the Day of Arafa. On the day before Tarwiya, the imam gives a sermon teaching people about going out to Mina, the prayer at Arafat, the standing (wuquf) there, and the ifada (leaving it together).

cards.title: To Mina, then Arafat
cards.ar: فإذا صلى الفجر يوم التروية بمكة خرج إلى منى فأقام بها حتى يصلي الفجر يوم عرفة ثم يتوجه إلى عرفات فيقيم بها
cards.en: After praying Fajr in Makkah on the Day of Tarwiya, he goes out to Mina and stays there until he has prayed Fajr on the Day of Arafa. Then he goes on to Arafat and stays there.

cards.ask: On the Day of Tarwiya, Khalid prays Fajr in Makkah. Where does he pray Fajr the next morning?
cards.source: خرج إلى منى فأقام بها حتى يصلي الفجر يوم عرفة
cards.why: He stays in Mina until he has prayed Fajr on the Day of Arafa, then goes to Arafat.

cards.title: Zuhr and Asr together at Arafa
cards.ar: فإذا زالت الشمس من يوم عرفة صلى الإمام بالناس الظهر والعصر ثم يبتدئ فيخطب خطبتين قبل الصلاة يعلم الناس فيها الصلاة والوقوف بعرفة والمزدلفة ورمي الجمار والنحر والحلق وطواف الزيارة
cards.en: When the sun passes its highest point (zawal) on the Day of Arafa, the imam leads Zuhr and Asr. Before the prayer he gives two sermons, teaching the prayer, the standing at Arafa and Muzdalifa, throwing the pebbles, the sacrifice, shaving, and tawaf al-ziyara.

cards.title: Joined in Zuhr's time
cards.ar: ويصلي بهم الظهر والعصر في وقت الظهر بأذان
cards.en: He leads them in Zuhr and Asr together in Zuhr's time, with one adhan and two iqamas. Someone who prays alone in his tent prays each in its own time, for Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the one alone also joins them.

cards.ask: Ibrahim prays alone in his tent at Arafa instead of with the imam. For Abu Hanifa, how does he pray Zuhr and Asr?
cards.source: ومن صلى في رحله وحده صلى كل واحدة منهما في وقتها عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, the one who prays alone in his tent prays each prayer in its own time.

cards.title: Where to stand
cards.ar: ثم يتوجه إلى الموقف فيقف بقرب الجبل وعرفات كلها موقف إلا بطن عرنة
cards.en: Then he goes to the standing place and stands near the mountain. All of Arafat is a place to stand, except Batn 'Urana (a valley at its edge).

cards.ask: Musa spends the afternoon of Arafa standing in Batn 'Urana. Is that a place of standing?
options: No: all Arafat is, except Batn 'Urana
Yes, if he faces the mountain
cards.source: وعرفات كلها موقف إلا بطن عرنة
cards.why: Batn 'Urana is the one part excluded from the standing place.

cards.title: The imam's standing, and du'a
cards.ar: وينبغي للإمام أن يقف بعرفة على راحلته ويدعو ويعلم الناس المناسك ويستحب أن يغتسل قبل الوقوف ويجتهد في الدعاء
cards.en: The imam should stand at Arafa on his mount, making du'a and teaching people the rites. It is liked to take a ghusl before the standing, and to try hard in du'a.

cards.ask: Put these in order, from the Day of Tarwiya.
steps: Go out to Mina and stay there
Pray Fajr of the Day of Arafa in Mina
Pray Zuhr and Asr together after zawal
Stand near the mountain and make du'a
source: فإذا صلى الفجر يوم التروية بمكة خرج إلى منى فأقام بها حتى يصلي الفجر يوم عرفة ثم يتوجه إلى عرفات
ويصلي بهم الظهر والعصر في وقت الظهر
ثم يتوجه إلى الموقف فيقف بقرب الجبل
cards.why: Fajr in Makkah, Mina overnight, Fajr in Mina, then Arafat: the joined prayers after zawal, then the standing.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The imam gives two sermons on the Day of Arafa
The joined prayers are in Zuhr's time
A ghusl before the standing is liked
All of Arafat including Batn 'Urana is a place to stand
He goes from Makkah straight to Arafat on the Day of Tarwiya

source: فيخطب خطبتين قبل الصلاة
ويصلي بهم الظهر والعصر في وقت الظهر
ويستحب أن يغتسل قبل الوقوف
إلا بطن عرنة
خرج إلى منى فأقام بها
cards.why: Two sermons, the joined prayers in Zuhr's time, and a ghusl before standing. Batn 'Urana is excluded, and Tarwiya night is in Mina.

cards.title: Leaving Arafat after sunset
cards.ar: فإذا غربت الشمس أفاض الإمام والناس معه على هينتهم حتى يأتوا المزدلفة فينزلوا بها
cards.en: When the sun sets, the imam leaves Arafat and the people go with him, calmly, until they reach Muzdalifa and stop there.

cards.ask: When do the pilgrims leave Arafat?
cards.source: فإذا غربت الشمس أفاض الإمام والناس معه
cards.why: They leave once the sun has set, going with the imam.

cards.title: Near Quzah
cards.ar: والمستحب أن ينزل بقرب الجبل الذي عليه الميقدة يقال له قزح
cards.en: It is liked to stop near the hill with the fire-beacon on it, called Quzah.

cards.title: Maghrib and Isha
cards.ar: ويصلي الإمام بالناس المغرب والعشاء بأذان وإقامة ومن صلى المغرب في الطريق لم يجز عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.en: At Muzdalifa the imam leads Maghrib and Isha together with one adhan and one iqama. Whoever prays Maghrib on the way there, it does not count, for Abu Hanifa and Muhammad.

cards.ask: Tariq prays Maghrib on the road, before reaching Muzdalifa. For Abu Hanifa, does it count?
options: Yes: Maghrib's time had come in
Yes, if he prays Isha there too
cards.source: ومن صلى المغرب في الطريق لم يجز عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa and Muhammad, Maghrib prayed on the way does not count. It is prayed at Muzdalifa.

cards.ask: Complete it: how are Maghrib and Isha called at Muzdalifa?
cards.ar: ويصلي الإمام بالناس المغرب والعشاء بأذان ____
cards.source: ويصلي الإمام بالناس المغرب والعشاء بأذان وإقامة
cards.why: One adhan and one iqama. (At Arafa it was one adhan and two iqamas.)

cards.title: Fajr and the standing
cards.ar: فإذا طلع الفجر صلى الإمام بالناس الفجر بغلس ثم وقف ووقف الناس معه فدعا: والمزدلفة كلها موقف إلا بطن محسر
cards.en: At dawn the imam leads Fajr at ghalas (while it is still dark). Then he stands and the people stand with him, making du'a. All of Muzdalifa is a place to stand except Batn Muhassir (a valley beside it).

cards.title: On to Mina before sunrise
cards.ar: ثم أفاض الإمام والناس معه قبل طلوع الشمس حتى يأتوا منى
cards.en: Then the imam and the people leave before sunrise and go to Mina.

cards.ask: Put the night and morning in order.
steps: Pray Fajr while it is still dark
source: فإذا غربت الشمس أفاض الإمام والناس معه
حتى يأتوا المزدلفة فينزلوا بها
ويصلي الإمام بالناس المغرب والعشاء
صلى الإمام بالناس الفجر بغلس ثم وقف
ثم أفاض الإمام والناس معه قبل طلوع الشمس حتى يأتوا منى
cards.why: Sunset at Arafat, then Muzdalifa: Maghrib and Isha, Fajr in the dark, the standing, and off to Mina before sunrise.

cards.ask: A place of standing or not?
source: والمزدلفة كلها موقف إلا بطن محسر
وعرفات كلها موقف إلا بطن عرنة
cards.why: All of Muzdalifa except Batn Muhassir, and all of Arafat except Batn 'Urana.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: They leave Arafat calmly
Fajr at Muzdalifa is prayed while still dark
They leave Muzdalifa before sunrise
Maghrib and Isha at Muzdalifa have two adhans
They leave Muzdalifa after sunrise

source: على هينتهم
الفجر بغلس
قبل طلوع الشمس
بأذان وإقامة
cards.why: Calmly from Arafat, Fajr in the dark, and away before sunrise. Maghrib and Isha have one adhan and one iqama.

cards.title: Jamrat al-'Aqaba
cards.ar: فيبتدئ بجمرة العقبة فيرميها من بطن الوادي بسبع حصيات مثل الخذف
cards.en: A jamra is one of the stone pillars in Mina that pilgrims throw pebbles at. On reaching Mina he starts with Jamrat al-'Aqaba, throwing at it from the valley bottom seven pebbles, small like those flicked between the fingers.

cards.title: Takbir, and the talbiya stops
cards.ar: ويكبر مع كل حصاة ولا يقف عندها ويقطع التلبية مع أول حصاة
cards.en: He says "Allahu akbar" with each pebble and does not stop there afterwards. He stops saying the talbiya with the first pebble.

cards.ask: When does the pilgrim doing Hajj stop the talbiya?
options: With the first pebble at Jamrat al-'Aqaba
After the last pebble on the last day
cards.source: ويقطع التلبية مع أول حصاة
cards.why: He keeps the talbiya until he throws the first pebble at Jamrat al-'Aqaba.

cards.title: Sacrifice and shaving
cards.ar: ثم يذبح إن أحب ثم يحلق أو يقصر والحلق أفضل وقد حل له كل شيء إلا النساء
cards.en: Then he sacrifices if he wishes, then shaves his head or cuts his hair short, and shaving is better. Now everything is allowed for him again except his wife.

cards.ask: Anas has thrown at Jamrat al-'Aqaba and shaved his head. What is still not allowed for him?
cards.source: وقد حل له كل شيء إلا النساء
cards.why: After shaving everything is allowed except his wife, until tawaf al-ziyara.

cards.title: Tawaf al-ziyara
cards.ar: ثم يأتي مكة من يومه ذلك أو من الغد أو من بعد الغد فيطوف بالبيت طواف الزيارة
cards.en: Then he goes to Makkah that same day, or the next, or the one after, and walks round the House: this is tawaf al-ziyara (the visiting tawaf), seven circuits.

cards.title: Ramal and sa'y in it
cards.ar: فإن كان سعى بين الصفا والمروة عقيب طواف القدوم لم يرمل في هذا الطواف ولا سعي عليه وإن لم يكن قدم السعي رمل في هذا الطواف وسعى بعده على ما قدمناه
cards.en: If he already did sa'y after tawaf al-qudum, he does no ramal in this tawaf and has no sa'y. If he did not do sa'y earlier, he does ramal in this tawaf and sa'y after it, as described before.

cards.ask: Yusuf did sa'y after his tawaf al-qudum. What about ramal and sa'y with tawaf al-ziyara?
cards.source: فإن كان سعى بين الصفا والمروة عقيب طواف القدوم لم يرمل في هذا الطواف ولا سعي عليه
cards.why: His sa'y is already done, so this tawaf has no ramal and no sa'y after it.

cards.title: The fard tawaf
cards.ar: وقد حل له النساء وهذا الطواف هو المفروض في الحج ويكره تأخيره عن هذه الأيام فإن أخره عنها لزمه دم عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: After it his wife is allowed to him too. This tawaf is the fard (obligatory pillar) of Hajj. It is makruh (disliked) to put it off past these days; for Abu Hanifa, whoever does must give a dam (slaughter a sheep or goat).

cards.ask: Put the rites of the Day of Sacrifice in order.
steps: Throw seven pebbles at Jamrat al-'Aqaba
Go to Makkah for tawaf al-ziyara
source: فيبتدئ بجمرة العقبة فيرميها
ثم يذبح إن أحب ثم يحلق أو يقصر
ثم يأتي مكة من يومه ذلك
cards.why: Throwing, then sacrifice, then shaving, then tawaf al-ziyara.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Shaving is better than cutting short
Tawaf al-ziyara is the fard tawaf of Hajj
He does not stop at Jamrat al-'Aqaba after throwing
Tawaf al-ziyara must be on the Day of Sacrifice itself
After shaving, his wife is allowed to him

source: والحلق أفضل
وهذا الطواف هو المفروض في الحج
ولا يقف عندها
من يومه ذلك أو من الغد أو من بعد الغد
إلا النساء
cards.why: Shaving is better, al-ziyara is the fard, and he does not stop at al-'Aqaba. Al-ziyara may be that day or the two after, and his wife is allowed only after it.

lessons.title: The days in Mina, and the farewell

cards.title: The first jamra
cards.ar: ثم يعود إلى منى فيقيم بها فإذا زالت الشمس من اليوم الثاني من النحر رمى الجمار الثلاث يبتدئ بالتي تلي المسجد فيرميها بسبع حصيات يكبر مع كل حصاة ويقف ويدعو عندها
cards.en: He goes back to Mina and stays there. On the second day of the sacrifice days, after zawal, he throws at all three jamras. He starts with the one next to the Masjid: seven pebbles, takbir with each, then he stands there making du'a.

cards.title: The middle one, then al-'Aqaba
cards.ar: ثم يرمي التي تليها مثل ذلك ويقف عندها ثم يرمي جمرة العقبة كذلك ولا يقف عندها
cards.en: Then he throws at the next one in the same way and stands there. Then he throws at Jamrat al-'Aqaba the same way, but does not stand there.

cards.ask: Put the three jamras in order.
steps: The jamra next to the Masjid, then stand and make du'a
source: يبتدئ بالتي تلي المسجد
ثم يرمي التي تليها مثل ذلك ويقف عندها ثم يرمي جمرة العقبة كذلك ولا يقف عندها
cards.why: He starts next to the Masjid, then the middle one, and ends at al-'Aqaba, where he does not stand.

cards.ask: Bilal has thrown at all three jamras. At which one does he not stand for du'a?
options: The one next to the Masjid
cards.source: ثم يرمي جمرة العقبة كذلك ولا يقف عندها
cards.why: He stands after the first two, but not after Jamrat al-'Aqaba.

cards.title: The third and fourth days
cards.ar: فإذا كان من الغد رمى الجمار الثلاث بعد زوال الشمس كذلك فإذا أراد أن يتعجل النفر نفر إلى مكة وإن أراد أن يقيم رمى الجمار الثلاث في يوم الرابع بعد زوال الشمس
cards.en: The next day he again throws at the three jamras after zawal. If he wants to leave early, he leaves for Makkah. If he wants to stay, he throws at the three on the fourth day, after zawal.

cards.title: Throwing early on the fourth day
cards.ar: فإن قدم الرمي في هذا اليوم قبل الزوال بعد طلوع الفجر جاز عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله
cards.en: If on that fourth day he throws before zawal but after dawn, it counts, for Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: Yahya stays in Mina for the fourth day and throws his pebbles in the morning, after Fajr but before zawal. For Abu Hanifa, does it count?
options: Yes, on this day it does
Only if he throws again after zawal
cards.source: فإن قدم الرمي في هذا اليوم قبل الزوال بعد طلوع الفجر جاز عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: On the fourth day, throwing after dawn and before zawal counts for Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: The farewell tawaf
cards.ar: ويكره أن يقدم الإنسان ثقله إلى مكة ويقيم بها حتى يرمي فإذا نفر إلى مكة نزل بالمحصب ثم طاف بالبيت سبعة أشواط لا يرمل فيها وهذا طواف الصدر هو واجب إلا على أهل مكة ثم يعود إلى أهله
cards.en: It is makruh to send his baggage ahead to Makkah while he stays to throw. When he leaves for Makkah he stops at al-Muhassab, then walks round the House seven circuits without ramal. This is tawaf al-sadr (the farewell tawaf). It is wajib, except on the people of Makkah. Then he goes home.

cards.ask: Hind lives in Makkah and has finished her Hajj. Must she do tawaf al-sadr?
options: No: it is not on the people of Makkah
Yes: it is wajib on everyone
cards.source: وهذا طواف الصدر هو واجب إلا على أهل مكة
cards.why: The farewell tawaf is wajib on everyone except the people of Makkah.

cards.ask: Which tawaf is it?
items: Done when leaving, before going home
Wajib, except on the people of Makkah
After it his wife is allowed to him
source: وهذا الطواف هو المفروض في الحج
وهذا طواف الصدر هو واجب إلا على أهل مكة ثم يعود إلى أهله
وقد حل له النساء
cards.why: Al-ziyara is the fard and makes his wife allowed. Al-sadr is the wajib farewell, done before going home.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: On the second day he throws after zawal
He may leave Mina before the fourth day
Tawaf al-sadr has no ramal
Sending one's baggage ahead to Makkah is liked
He starts the three jamras with al-'Aqaba

source: فإذا زالت الشمس من اليوم الثاني من النحر رمى الجمار الثلاث
فإذا أراد أن يتعجل النفر نفر إلى مكة
لا يرمل فيها
ويكره أن يقدم الإنسان ثقله إلى مكة
يبتدئ بالتي تلي المسجد
cards.why: After zawal, an early leave is allowed, and no ramal in the farewell. Sending baggage ahead is makruh, and he starts next to the Masjid.

lessons.title: Catching Arafa, and the woman's Hajj

cards.title: Going straight to Arafat
cards.ar: فإن لم يدخل المحرم مكة وتوجه إلى عرفات ووقف بها على ما قدمناه فقد سقط عنه طواف القدوم ولا شيء عليه لتركه
cards.en: If the pilgrim in ihram does not enter Makkah but goes straight to Arafat and stands there, tawaf al-qudum drops from him, and he owes nothing for missing it.

cards.ask: Ali arrives late and goes straight to Arafat without entering Makkah. What does he owe for missing tawaf al-qudum?
cards.source: فقد سقط عنه طواف القدوم ولا شيء عليه لتركه
cards.why: Tawaf al-qudum drops from him and he owes nothing for it.

cards.title: The time of the standing
cards.ar: ومن أدرك الوقوف بعرفة ما بين زوال الشمس من يوم عرفة إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر فقد أدرك الحج
cards.en: Whoever is at Arafa at any time from zawal on the Day of Arafa until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice has caught the Hajj.

cards.ask: Hamza's flight is delayed. He reaches Arafat at 2 a.m., in the night before the Day of Sacrifice, and stands a few minutes. Has he caught the Hajj?
options: Yes: it is before dawn of the Day of Sacrifice
No: he had to be there by sunset
No: he had to be there before Asr
cards.source: ما بين زوال الشمس من يوم عرفة إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر فقد أدرك الحج
cards.why: The time lasts until dawn of the Day of Sacrifice, so standing in the night still catches it.

cards.ask: Complete it: when does the standing's time begin?
cards.ar: ما بين ____ من يوم عرفة إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر
cards.source: ما بين زوال الشمس من يوم عرفة إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر
cards.why: From zawal on the Day of Arafa until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.

cards.title: Passing through asleep
cards.ar: ومن اجتاز بعرفة وهو نائم أو مغمى عليه أو لم يعلم أنها عرفة أجزأه ذلك عن الوقوف
cards.en: Whoever passes through Arafa asleep, or unconscious, or not knowing it is Arafa, that counts as his standing.

cards.ask: Sulayman falls asleep on the bus and it drives through Arafa in the afternoon of the Day of Arafa. Does that count as his standing?
options: No: he must know it is Arafa
cards.source: ومن اجتاز بعرفة وهو نائم أو مغمى عليه أو لم يعلم أنها عرفة أجزأه ذلك عن الوقوف
cards.why: Passing through asleep, unconscious or unaware still counts.

cards.title: The woman's Hajj
cards.ar: والمرأة في جميع ذلك كالرجل غير أنها لا تكشف رأسها وتكشف وجهها ولا ترفع صوتها بالتلبية ولا ترمل في الطواف ولا تسعى بين الميلين ولا تحلق رأسها ولكن تقصر
cards.en: A woman does all of this like a man, except: she does not uncover her head, but uncovers her face; she does not raise her voice in the talbiya; she does no ramal in tawaf; she does not run between the green markers; and she does not shave her head, but cuts it short.

cards.ask: Man or woman?
items: Raises his voice in the talbiya
Does ramal in the first three circuits
Walks the whole way between the green markers
Cuts the hair short rather than shaving
cards.source: غير أنها لا تكشف رأسها وتكشف وجهها ولا ترفع صوتها بالتلبية ولا ترمل في الطواف ولا تسعى بين الميلين ولا تحلق رأسها ولكن تقصر
cards.why: She keeps her head covered, does no ramal or running, keeps her talbiya quiet, and cuts rather than shaves.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: A woman in ihram uncovers her face
Standing at Arafa in the night before the Day of Sacrifice catches the Hajj
Missing tawaf al-qudum by going straight to Arafat costs nothing
Someone unconscious at Arafa has not stood
A woman shaves her head like a man

source: وتكشف وجهها
إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر فقد أدرك الحج
ولا شيء عليه لتركه
أو مغمى عليه
ولا تحلق رأسها ولكن تقصر
cards.why: Her face is uncovered, the night still counts, and missing al-qudum costs nothing. Unconscious still counts, and she cuts rather than shaves.

cards.title: Qiran is best
cards.ar: القران أفضل عندنا من التمتع والإفراد وصفة القران:
cards.en: There are three ways to do Hajj. Ifrad: Hajj alone. Tamattu': an umrah, coming out of ihram, then Hajj. Qiran: umrah and Hajj together in one ihram. For us (the Hanafis), qiran is the best of the three. The qarin enters ihram for both together at the miqat.

cards.ask: What does the qarin enter ihram for at the miqat? Complete it.
cards.ar: ____ معا
source: بالعمرة والحج معا
اللهم إني أريد الحج والعمرة
cards.why: He enters ihram for umrah and Hajj together, and says "I want Hajj and umrah".

cards.title: His du'a
cards.ar: ويقول عقيب صلاته: اللهم إني أريد الحج والعمرة فيسرهما لي وتقبلهما مني
cards.en: After his prayer he says: "O Allah, I want Hajj and umrah, so make them easy for me and accept them from me."

cards.title: The umrah first
cards.ar: فإذا دخل مكة ابتدأ فطاف بالبيت سبعة أشواط يرمل في الثلاث الأول منها
cards.en: On entering Makkah he first walks round the House seven circuits, with ramal in the first three, then does sa'y between Safa and Marwa. These are the acts of the umrah.

cards.title: Then the Hajj's tawaf and sa'y
cards.ar: ثم يطوف بعد السعي طواف القدوم ويسعى بين الصفا والمروة كما بينا في المفرد
cards.en: After that sa'y he does tawaf al-qudum and another sa'y, as described for the mufrid.

cards.ask: Put the qarin's acts in Makkah in order.
steps: Tawaf of the umrah, with ramal
source: فإذا دخل مكة ابتدأ فطاف بالبيت سبعة أشواط
بين الصفا والمروة وهذه أفعال العمرة
ثم يطوف بعد السعي طواف القدوم ويسعى بين الصفا والمروة
cards.why: The umrah's tawaf and sa'y come first, then the Hajj's tawaf al-qudum and its sa'y.

cards.title: The dam of qiran
cards.ar: فإذا رمى الجمرة يوم النحر ذبح شاة أو بقرة أو بدنة
cards.en: After throwing at the jamra on the Day of Sacrifice, he slaughters a sheep, a cow, or a badana (a camel), or a seventh share of a badana. This is the dam of qiran.

cards.title: If he has no animal
cards.ar: فإن لم يكن له ما يذبح صام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وآخرها يوم عرفة فإن فاته الصوم حتى جاء يوم النحر لم يجزه إلا الدم ثم يصوم سبعة أيام إذا رجع إلى أهله وإن صامها بمكة بعد فراغه من الحج جاز
cards.en: If he has nothing to slaughter, he fasts three days during Hajj, the last being the Day of Arafa, and seven more when he gets home. If he fasts those seven in Makkah after finishing Hajj, that counts too. But if he misses the three fasts until the Day of Sacrifice comes, only the dam will do.

cards.ask: Hassan is a qarin with no animal to slaughter. How many days does he fast altogether?
options: Ten: three during Hajj and seven after
cards.source: صام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وآخرها يوم عرفة فإن فاته الصوم حتى جاء يوم النحر لم يجزه إلا الدم ثم يصوم سبعة أيام إذا رجع إلى أهله
cards.why: Three days during Hajj, ending on the Day of Arafa, plus seven after: ten in all.

cards.ask: Idris had no animal, but did not fast the three days, and now the Day of Sacrifice has come. What will do for him now?
options: Fasting three days in the days of Mina
cards.source: فإن فاته الصوم حتى جاء يوم النحر لم يجزه إلا الدم
cards.why: Once the Day of Sacrifice comes with the three fasts missed, nothing but the dam will do.

cards.ask: Umar, a qarin, does not enter Makkah but goes straight to Arafat and stands. What happens?
options: He has dropped his umrah: a dam for that, he makes it up, and no dam of qiran
cards.source: فقد صار رافضا لعمرته بالوقوف وبطل عنه دم القران وعليه دم لرفض عمرته وعليه قضاؤها
cards.why: Standing at Arafat before his umrah means he has dropped the umrah. The dam of qiran falls away, he owes a dam for dropping the umrah, and he must make it up.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Qiran is the best way, for the Hanafis
The qarin's umrah tawaf has ramal
The three fasts end on the Day of Arafa
The seven fasts may never be done in Makkah
The qarin does sa'y only once

source: القران أفضل عندنا من التمتع والإفراد
يرمل في الثلاث الأول منها
وآخرها يوم عرفة
وإن صامها بمكة بعد فراغه من الحج جاز
ثم يطوف بعد السعي طواف القدوم ويسعى
cards.why: Qiran is best, the umrah tawaf has ramal, and the three fasts end on Arafa. The seven may be fasted in Makkah after Hajj, and he does two sa'ys.

cards.title: Better than ifrad, and its two kinds
cards.ar: التمتع أفضل من الإفراد عندنا والتمتع على وجهين: ومتمتع يسوق الهدي
