cards.en: Tamattu' is better than ifrad, for us. It comes in two kinds: a mutamatti' who drives a hady along, and one who does not. A hady is an animal brought to be sacrificed in the Haram.

cards.ask: Which order is right, best first, for the Hanafis?
source: القران أفضل عندنا من التمتع والإفراد
التمتع أفضل من الإفراد عندنا
cards.why: Qiran is better than both, and tamattu' is better than ifrad.

cards.title: How tamattu' is done
cards.ar: وصفة التمتع: أن يبتدئ من الميقات فيحرم بعمرة ويدخل مكة فيطوف لها ويسعى ويحلق أو يقصر وقد حل من عمرته
cards.en: He starts at the miqat by entering ihram for an umrah. He enters Makkah, does its tawaf and sa'y, and shaves or cuts his hair. Now he is out of the ihram of his umrah.

cards.title: Then the Hajj
cards.ar: ويقطع التلبية إذا ابتدأ بالطواف ويقيم بمكة حلالا فإذا كان يوم التروية أحرم بالحج من المسجد وفعل ما يفعله الحاج المفرد وعليه دم التمتع فإن لم يجد صام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجع
cards.en: He stops the talbiya when he begins the umrah's tawaf, and stays in Makkah out of ihram. On the Day of Tarwiya he enters ihram for Hajj from the Masjid and does what the mufrid does. He owes the dam of tamattu'; if he has none, he fasts three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.

cards.ask: Put tamattu' (without a hady) in order.
steps: Enter ihram for umrah at the miqat
Stay in Makkah out of ihram
Enter ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiya
source: أن يبتدئ من الميقات فيحرم بعمرة ويدخل مكة فيطوف لها ويسعى ويحلق أو يقصر
ويقيم بمكة حلالا فإذا كان يوم التروية أحرم بالحج من المسجد
cards.why: Umrah ihram, tawaf, sa'y, shaving, a break out of ihram in Makkah, then Hajj ihram on Tarwiya.

cards.ask: Bilal is doing tamattu'. When does he stop the talbiya of his umrah?
cards.source: ويقطع التلبية إذا ابتدأ بالطواف
cards.why: For the umrah the talbiya stops as the tawaf begins.

cards.title: Driving a hady
cards.ar: وإذا أراد المتمتع أن يسوق الهدي أحرم وساق هديه فإن كانت بدنة قلدها بمزادة أو نعل
cards.en: If he wants to drive a hady, he enters ihram and drives it along. If it is a badana, he garlands it, hanging a leather water bag or a sandal on its neck. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he also does ish'ar (cuts its hump on the right side to mark it); Abu Hanifa says he does not.

cards.title: He stays in ihram
cards.ar: فإذا دخل مكة طاف وسعى ولم يتحلل حتى يحرم بالحج يوم التروية وإن قدم الإحرام قبله جاز وعليه دم فإذا حلق يوم النحر فقد حل من الإحرامين
cards.en: When he enters Makkah he does tawaf and sa'y but does not come out of ihram. He enters ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiya (earlier is allowed too). He owes a dam. When he shaves on the Day of Sacrifice he comes out of both ihrams.

cards.ask: A mutamatti' who drives a hady, or one who does not?
items: Comes out of ihram after the umrah
Stays in ihram until the Day of Sacrifice
Hangs a sandal on his camel's neck
Stays in Makkah out of ihram until Tarwiya
source: ويحلق أو يقصر وقد حل من عمرته
ولم يتحلل حتى يحرم بالحج يوم التروية
فإن كانت بدنة قلدها بمزادة أو نعل
ويقيم بمكة حلالا
cards.why: Without a hady he comes out of ihram after the umrah. With one, he stays in ihram until he shaves on the Day of Sacrifice.

cards.ask: Faisal lives in Makkah. He wants to do tamattu' this year. What is open to him?
cards.source: وليس لأهل مكة تمتع ولا قران وإنما لهم الإفراد خاصة
cards.why: The people of Makkah have no tamattu' and no qiran; for them it is ifrad only.

cards.ask: Idris from Madinah does an umrah in Shawwal with no hady, goes home to Madinah, and comes back for Hajj that year. Is he a mutamatti'?
options: No: going home in between ends his tamattu'
Yes: both were in the same year
Yes, if he gives a dam
cards.source: إلى أهله بعد فراغه من العمرة ولم يكن ساق الهدي بطل تمتعه
cards.why: Without a hady, returning to his family after the umrah cancels the tamattu'.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The mutamatti' enters ihram for Hajj from the Masjid
He owes the dam of tamattu'
With a hady, he comes out of both ihrams when he shaves on the Day of Sacrifice
The people of Makkah may do qiran
Without a hady, he stays in ihram between the umrah and the Hajj

source: أحرم بالحج من المسجد
وعليه دم التمتع
فإذا حلق يوم النحر فقد حل من الإحرامين
وليس لأهل مكة تمتع ولا قران
ويقيم بمكة حلالا
cards.why: Hajj ihram from the Masjid, the dam of tamattu', and a hady keeps him in ihram until he shaves. Makkans do ifrad only, and without a hady he is out of ihram in between.

lessons.title: The months of Hajj, and a woman's period

cards.title: An umrah begun before the months
cards.ar: ومن أحرم بالعمرة قبل أشهر الحج فطاف لها أقل من أربعة أشواط ثم دخلت أشهر الحج فتممها وأحرم بالحج كان متمتعا
cards.en: If someone enters ihram for umrah before the months of Hajj, does fewer than four circuits of its tawaf, and then the months of Hajj begin, and he finishes the umrah and enters ihram for Hajj, he is a mutamatti'.

cards.title: Four circuits or more
cards.ar: وإن طاف لعمرته قبل أشهر الحج أربعة أشواط فصاعدا ثم حج من عامه ذلك لم يكن متمتعا
cards.en: But if he did four circuits or more before the months of Hajj, and then does Hajj that same year, he is not a mutamatti'.

cards.ask: Umar enters ihram for umrah in Ramadan and does three circuits. Then Shawwal comes in. He finishes the umrah and later does Hajj. Is he a mutamatti'?
options: Yes: fewer than four were before the months
No: he began the umrah in Ramadan
cards.source: فطاف لها أقل من أربعة أشواط ثم دخلت أشهر الحج فتممها وأحرم بالحج كان متمتعا
cards.why: Fewer than four circuits came before the months, so he counts as a mutamatti'.

cards.ask: Zayd does five circuits of his umrah's tawaf in Ramadan, then does Hajj that year. Is he a mutamatti'?
options: No: four or more were before the months
Yes: the Hajj was that year
Yes, if he finishes the umrah in Shawwal
cards.source: وإن طاف لعمرته قبل أشهر الحج أربعة أشواط فصاعدا ثم حج من عامه ذلك لم يكن متمتعا
cards.why: Four or more circuits before the months means he is not a mutamatti'.

cards.title: The months of Hajj
cards.ar: وأشهر الحج: شوال وذو القعدة وعشر من ذي الحجة فإن قدم الإحرام بالحج عليها جاز إحرامه وانعقد حجا
cards.en: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'da, and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijja. If he enters ihram for Hajj before them, his ihram is valid and counts as a Hajj ihram.

cards.ask: Which of these are within the months of Hajj?

options.text: Shawwal
Dhul-Qa'da
The 5th of Dhul-Hijja
Ramadan
Muharram

cards.source: وأشهر الحج: شوال وذو القعدة وعشر من ذي الحجة
cards.why: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'da and the first ten of Dhul-Hijja. Ramadan and Muharram are outside them.

cards.ask: Salim enters ihram for Hajj in Ramadan. Is his ihram valid?
options: Yes, and it counts as a Hajj ihram
No: Hajj ihram is only in the months
cards.source: فإن قدم الإحرام بالحج عليها جاز إحرامه وانعقد حجا
cards.why: Entering Hajj ihram before its months is allowed, and it counts as Hajj.

cards.title: Her period during Hajj
cards.ar: غير أنها لا تطوف بالبيت حتى تطهر وإن حاضت بعد الوقوف وطواف الزيارة انصرفت من مكة ولا شيء عليها لترك طواف الصدر
cards.en: If a woman's period starts when she is entering ihram, she bathes, enters ihram and does all the pilgrim does, except that she does not walk round the House until she is clean. If her period starts after the standing and tawaf al-ziyara, she leaves Makkah and owes nothing for missing tawaf al-sadr.

cards.ask: Aisha's period starts at the miqat. What does she do?
options: Bathe, enter ihram, and do every rite except tawaf until she is clean
Wait at the miqat until she is clean
Enter ihram with no bath and skip Arafa
source: وإذا حاضت المرأة عند الإحرام اغتسلت وأحرمت
غير أنها لا تطوف بالبيت حتى تطهر
cards.why: She bathes and enters ihram and does all the rites. Only the tawaf waits until she is clean.

cards.ask: Maryam's period starts after she has stood at Arafa and done tawaf al-ziyara. Her group leaves Makkah. What does she owe for tawaf al-sadr?
options: She must wait to do it
cards.source: وإن حاضت بعد الوقوف وطواف الزيارة انصرفت من مكة ولا شيء عليها لترك طواف الصدر
cards.why: With the standing and al-ziyara done, she may leave and owes nothing for the farewell tawaf.

cards.ask: A mutamatti' or not?
items: Did 2 circuits of his umrah in Ramadan, finished it in Shawwal, then did Hajj
Did 4 circuits of his umrah in Ramadan, then did Hajj that year
Did umrah in Shawwal, stayed in Makkah, entered ihram for Hajj on Tarwiya
source: فطاف لها أقل من أربعة أشواط ثم دخلت أشهر الحج فتممها وأحرم بالحج كان متمتعا
أربعة أشواط فصاعدا ثم حج من عامه ذلك لم يكن متمتعا
وليس لأهل مكة تمتع
cards.why: Fewer than four circuits before the months still makes tamattu'; four or more does not. Makkans have no tamattu'.

lessons.title: The muhrim's wrongs: perfume, clothes, hair, nails

cards.title: Perfume
cards.ar: إذا تطيب المحرم فعليه الكفارة فإذا طيب عضوا كاملا فما زاد فعليه دم وإن طيب أقل من عضو فعليه صدقة
cards.en: A jinaya is a wrong done in ihram. If the muhrim wears perfume he owes a kaffara (a making-up). Perfume on a whole limb or more: a dam (a sheep slaughtered in the Haram). Less than a whole limb: a sadaqa (a charity).

cards.ask: Khalid, in ihram, rubs perfume over his whole arm. What does he owe?
cards.source: فإذا طيب عضوا كاملا فما زاد فعليه دم
cards.why: A whole limb or more means a dam.

cards.title: Sewn clothes and covering the head
cards.ar: وإن لبس ثوبا مخيطا أو غطى رأسه يوما كاملا فعليه دم وإن كان أقل من ذلك فعليه صدقة
cards.en: If he wears sewn clothing, or covers his head, for a whole day: a dam. Less than that: a sadaqa.

cards.title: Shaving
cards.ar: وإن حلق ربع رأسه فصاعدا فعليه دم وإن حلق أقل من الربع فعليه صدقة وإن حلق مواضع المحاجم فعليه دم عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Shaving a quarter of the head or more: a dam. Less than a quarter: a sadaqa. Shaving the places for cupping: a dam, for Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say a sadaqa.

cards.title: Nails
cards.ar: وإن قص أظافير يديه ورجليه فعليه دم وإن قص يدا أو رجلا فعليه دم وإن قص أقل من خمسة أظافير متفرقة من يديه ورجليه فعليه صدقة عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف
cards.en: Cutting the nails of both hands and feet: a dam. Of one hand or one foot: a dam. Fewer than five nails scattered over his hands and feet: a sadaqa, for Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf. Note: Muhammad says a dam.

cards.ask: A dam or a sadaqa?
items: Wore a shirt for a whole day
Covered his head for an hour
Shaved a quarter of his head
Cut all the nails of one hand
source: فإذا طيب عضوا كاملا فما زاد فعليه دم وإن طيب أقل من عضو فعليه صدقة
وإن لبس ثوبا مخيطا أو غطى رأسه يوما كاملا فعليه دم وإن كان أقل من ذلك فعليه صدقة
وإن حلق ربع رأسه فصاعدا فعليه دم
وإن قص يدا أو رجلا فعليه دم
cards.why: A whole limb, a whole day, a quarter of the head, a whole hand: a dam. Less than these: a sadaqa.

cards.ask: Hamza covers his head with a cloth for half a day in ihram. What does he owe?
cards.source: أو غطى رأسه يوما كاملا فعليه دم وإن كان أقل من ذلك فعليه صدقة
cards.why: Less than a whole day means a sadaqa.

cards.title: With an excuse
cards.ar: وإن تطيب أو حلق أو لبس من عذر فهو مخير: إن شاء ذبح شاة وإن شاء تصدق على ستة مساكين بثلاثة أصوع من طعام وإن شاء صام ثلاثة أيام
cards.en: If he used perfume, shaved or wore clothes because of an excuse (like illness), he has a choice: slaughter a sheep, or give three sa' (a sa' is a measure of grain) of food to six poor people, or fast three days.

cards.ask: Complete it: the food given to six poor people.
cards.ar: وإن شاء تصدق على ستة مساكين بثلاثة ____ من طعام
cards.source: وإن شاء تصدق على ستة مساكين بثلاثة أصوع من طعام
cards.why: Three sa' of food, shared among six poor people.

cards.ask: Ali gets a painful head illness in ihram and has to shave his head. Which choice does he have?
options: A sheep, or food for six poor people, or three days' fasting
cards.source: وإن تطيب أو حلق أو لبس من عذر فهو مخير
cards.why: With an excuse he chooses between the sheep, the food, and the three days' fasting.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Shaving less than a quarter of the head: a sadaqa
Cutting the nails of one foot: a dam
With an excuse, fasting three days is enough
Perfume on less than a limb: a dam
With an excuse, he must slaughter a sheep

source: وإن حلق أقل من الربع فعليه صدقة
وإن قص يدا أو رجلا فعليه دم
وإن شاء صام ثلاثة أيام
وإن طيب أقل من عضو فعليه صدقة
فهو مخير
cards.why: Less than a quarter is a sadaqa, one foot is a dam, and with an excuse fasting is one of his choices. Less than a limb is a sadaqa, and the sheep is only one option.

cards.title: Kissing and touching
cards.ar: وإن قبل أو لمس بشهوة فعليه دم
cards.en: If he kisses or touches his wife with desire while in ihram, he owes a dam.

cards.title: Before the standing at Arafa
cards.ar: ومن جامع في أحد السبيلين قبل الوقوف بعرفة فسد حجه وعليه شاة ويمضي في الحج كما يمضي من لم يفسد حجه وعليه القضاء وليس عليه أن يفارق امرأته إذا حج بها في القضاء
cards.en: If he has intercourse before standing at Arafa, his Hajj is spoiled. He owes a sheep, carries on with the Hajj as if it were not spoiled, and must make it up (qada') later. He does not have to keep apart from his wife when he takes her on the make-up Hajj.

cards.ask: Yasir has intercourse with his wife in ihram, before the standing at Arafa. What happens?
options: His Hajj is spoiled: a sheep, he carries on, and makes it up
Nothing is spoiled, but he owes a badana
He leaves ihram at once and goes home
cards.source: قبل الوقوف بعرفة فسد حجه وعليه شاة ويمضي في الحج كما يمضي من لم يفسد حجه وعليه القضاء
cards.why: Before Arafa it spoils the Hajj. He still finishes it, owes a sheep, and makes it up.

cards.title: After the standing
cards.ar: ومن جامع بعد الوقوف بعرفة لم يفسد حجه وعليه بدنة فإن جامع بعد الحلق فعليه شاة
cards.en: After the standing at Arafa, intercourse does not spoil the Hajj, but he owes a badana (a camel). If it is after shaving, he owes a sheep.

cards.ask: Nasir stood at Arafa, but has not yet shaved, when he has intercourse. What does he owe?
options: A badana, and his Hajj is not spoiled
A sheep, and his Hajj is spoiled
cards.source: ومن جامع بعد الوقوف بعرفة لم يفسد حجه وعليه بدنة
cards.why: After Arafa and before shaving: no spoiling, but a badana.

cards.title: In an umrah
cards.ar: أفسدها ومضى فيها وقضاها وعليه شاة وإن وطئ بعدها طاف أربعة أشواط فعليه شاة ولا تفسد عمرته ولا يلزمه قضاؤها
cards.en: In an umrah, intercourse before he has done four circuits of its tawaf spoils it: he carries on, makes it up, and owes a sheep. If it is after four circuits, he owes a sheep, but his umrah is not spoiled and he need not make it up.

cards.ask: Tariq is doing umrah and has done two circuits of the tawaf when he has intercourse. What happens?
options: The umrah is spoiled: he finishes it, makes it up, and owes a sheep
Nothing is spoiled; a sheep only
source: ومن جامع في العمرة
أفسدها ومضى فيها وقضاها وعليه شاة
cards.why: Before four circuits it spoils the umrah. He carries on, makes it up, and owes a sheep.

cards.title: Forgetting
cards.ar: ومن جامع ناسيا كمن جامع عامدا
cards.en: Whoever does it forgetting he is in ihram is like one who did it on purpose.

cards.ask: What does each one owe?
items: Intercourse after the standing, before shaving
Intercourse before Arafa (plus a make-up Hajj)
source: وعليه بدنة فإن جامع بعد الحلق فعليه شاة
قبل الوقوف بعرفة فسد حجه وعليه شاة
وإن قبل أو لمس بشهوة فعليه دم
وإن وطئ بعدها طاف أربعة أشواط فعليه شاة
cards.why: Only after Arafa and before shaving is it a badana. After shaving, before Arafa, and late in umrah it is a sheep. A kiss with desire is a dam.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Forgetting is the same as doing it on purpose
The make-up Hajj does not need the couple kept apart
After four circuits of umrah, the umrah is not spoiled
Intercourse after Arafa spoils the Hajj
A spoiled Hajj is abandoned on the spot

source: ومن جامع ناسيا كمن جامع عامدا
وليس عليه أن يفارق امرأته إذا حج بها في القضاء
ولا تفسد عمرته
لم يفسد حجه وعليه بدنة
ويمضي في الحج كما يمضي من لم يفسد حجه
cards.why: Forgetting counts the same, no separation is needed, and late in umrah nothing is spoiled. After Arafa the Hajj is not spoiled, and a spoiled one is still finished.

lessons.title: Tawaf without purity, or cut short

cards.title: Tawaf al-qudum
cards.ar: ومن طاف طواف القدوم محدثا فعليه صدقه وإن طاف جنبا فعليه شاة
cards.en: Muhdith means without wudu; junub means needing a ghusl. Whoever does tawaf al-qudum without wudu owes a sadaqa. Junub: a sheep.

cards.title: Tawaf al-ziyara
cards.ar: ومن طاف طواف الزيارة محدثا فعليه شاة وإن كان جنبا
cards.en: Whoever does tawaf al-ziyara without wudu owes a sheep. If he was junub: a badana.

cards.ask: Hamza did tawaf al-ziyara while junub and only realised later. What does he owe?
source: ومن طاف طواف الزيارة محدثا فعليه شاة وإن كان جنبا
من طاف طواف الزيارة جنبا ومن جامع بعد الوقوف بعرفة فإنه لا يجوز إلا بدنة
cards.why: Tawaf al-ziyara while junub needs a badana; a sheep is not enough here.

cards.title: Repeating it is better
cards.ar: بدنة والأفضل أن يعيد الطواف ما دام بمكة ولا ذبح عليه ومن طاف طواف الصدر محدثا فعليه صدقة وإن طاف جنبا فعليه شاة
cards.en: It is better for him to repeat the tawaf while he is still in Makkah, and then he owes no slaughter. Tawaf al-sadr without wudu: a sadaqa. Junub: a sheep.

cards.ask: Khalid realises in Makkah that he did tawaf al-ziyara without wudu. What is best?
options: Repeat the tawaf while in Makkah; then nothing is owed
Slaughter a sheep and not repeat it
Repeat it and also slaughter a sheep
cards.source: والأفضل أن يعيد الطواف ما دام بمكة ولا ذبح عليه
cards.why: Repeating it while in Makkah is better, and then there is no slaughter.

cards.ask: What does each one owe?
source: ومن طاف طواف القدوم محدثا فعليه صدقه وإن طاف جنبا فعليه شاة
ومن طاف طواف الزيارة محدثا فعليه شاة
ومن طاف طواف الصدر محدثا فعليه صدقة
cards.why: Al-qudum and al-sadr: a sadaqa without wudu, a sheep when junub. Al-ziyara, the fard: a sheep without wudu, a badana when junub.

cards.title: Leaving circuits out
cards.ar: ومن ترك من طواف الزيارة ثلاثة أشواط فما دونها فعليه شاة وإن ترك أربعة أشواط بقي محرما أبدا حتى يطوفها ومن ترك ثلاثة أشواط من طواف الصدر فعليه صدقة وإن ترك طواف الصدر أو أربعة أشواط منه فعليه شاة
cards.en: Leaving out three circuits of tawaf al-ziyara or fewer: a sheep. Leaving out four: he stays in ihram for ever until he does them. Leaving out three circuits of tawaf al-sadr: a sadaqa. Leaving out tawaf al-sadr, or four circuits of it: a sheep.

cards.ask: Ali did only three circuits of tawaf al-ziyara and went home. What is his state?
options: Still in ihram, until he does the circuits
cards.source: وإن ترك أربعة أشواط بقي محرما أبدا حتى يطوفها
cards.why: He left four of the seven, so he stays a muhrim until he completes them.

cards.ask: Musa leaves Makkah without doing tawaf al-sadr at all. What does he owe?
cards.source: وإن ترك طواف الصدر أو أربعة أشواط منه فعليه شاة
cards.why: Leaving out the farewell tawaf, or four circuits of it, means a sheep.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Leaving two circuits of al-ziyara: a sheep
Leaving three circuits of al-sadr: a sadaqa
Repeating al-ziyara in Makkah removes the slaughter
Al-qudum without wudu: a sheep
Leaving four circuits of al-ziyara: a badana, then he is free

source: ثلاثة أشواط فما دونها فعليه شاة
ومن ترك ثلاثة أشواط من طواف الصدر فعليه صدقة
ولا ذبح عليه
ومن طاف طواف القدوم محدثا فعليه صدقه
بقي محرما أبدا حتى يطوفها
cards.why: Two circuits of al-ziyara is a sheep, three of al-sadr is a sadaqa, and repeating removes the slaughter. Al-qudum without wudu is only a sadaqa, and four circuits of al-ziyara keep him in ihram.

cards.title: Leaving out sa'y
cards.ar: ومن ترك السعي بين الصفا والمروة فعليه شاة وحجه تام
cards.en: Whoever leaves out sa'y between Safa and Marwa owes a sheep, and his Hajj is complete.

cards.ask: Salim forgets to do sa'y and goes home. What is the ruling?
options: He owes a sheep, and his Hajj is complete
He stays in ihram until he does it
cards.source: ومن ترك السعي بين الصفا والمروة فعليه شاة وحجه تام
cards.why: Sa'y is not a pillar: a sheep makes up for it and the Hajj stands.

cards.title: Leaving Arafa before the imam
cards.ar: قبل الإمام فعليه دم ومن ترك الوقوف بالمزدلفة فعليه دم
cards.en: Whoever leaves Arafa before the imam (that is, before sunset) owes a dam. Whoever leaves out the standing at Muzdalifa owes a dam.

cards.title: Leaving out the throwing
cards.ar: ومن ترك رمي الجمار في الأيام كلها فعليه دم وإن ترك رمي يوم واحد فعليه دم وإن ترك رمي إحدى الجمار الثلاث فعليه صدقة وإن ترك رمي جمرة العقبة في يوم النحر فعليه دم
cards.en: Leaving out the throwing on all the days: one dam. Leaving out one day's throwing: a dam. Leaving out one of the three jamras: a sadaqa. Leaving out Jamrat al-'Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice: a dam.

cards.ask: Ibrahim was ill and missed the throwing on every day. What does he owe?
cards.source: ومن ترك رمي الجمار في الأيام كلها فعليه دم
cards.why: Missing the throwing on all the days still means a single dam.

cards.ask: Yusuf threw at two of the three jamras on the third day but missed one. What does he owe?
cards.source: وإن ترك رمي إحدى الجمار الثلاث فعليه صدقة
cards.why: Missing one of the three jamras is a sadaqa.

cards.title: Putting off shaving and al-ziyara
cards.ar: حتى مضت أيام النحر فعليه دم عند أبي حنيفة وكذلك لو أخر طواف الزيارة عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله
cards.en: Whoever puts off his shaving until the days of sacrifice have passed owes a dam, for Abu Hanifa. So too if he puts off tawaf al-ziyara.

cards.ask: Hamid delays tawaf al-ziyara until after the days of sacrifice have ended. For Abu Hanifa, what does he owe?
options: Nothing: he did it in the end
cards.source: وكذلك لو أخر طواف الزيارة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, putting off al-ziyara past those days means a dam.

cards.ask: A dam or a sadaqa?
items: Missed one of the three jamras
Missed Jamrat al-'Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice
source: قبل الإمام فعليه دم
ومن ترك الوقوف بالمزدلفة فعليه دم
وإن ترك رمي يوم واحد فعليه دم وإن ترك رمي إحدى الجمار الثلاث فعليه صدقة وإن ترك رمي جمرة العقبة في يوم النحر فعليه دم
cards.why: Each of these is a dam, except missing just one of the three jamras, which is a sadaqa.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Missing sa'y does not void the Hajj
Leaving out Muzdalifa needs a dam
For Abu Hanifa, delaying shaving past the days of sacrifice needs a dam
Missing all the throwing needs a dam for each day
Leaving Arafa before the imam costs nothing

source: وحجه تام
ومن ترك الوقوف بالمزدلفة فعليه دم
حتى مضت أيام النحر فعليه دم عند أبي حنيفة
ومن ترك رمي الجمار في الأيام كلها فعليه دم
قبل الإمام فعليه دم
cards.why: Sa'y missed: the Hajj stands. Muzdalifa and delayed shaving: a dam. All the throwing is one dam, and leaving Arafa early is a dam.

cards.title: The jaza
cards.ar: وإذا قتل المحرم صيدا أو دل عليه من قتله فعليه الجزاء يستوي في ذلك العامد والناسي والمبتدئ والعائد
cards.en: If a muhrim kills game (a wild land animal), or shows it to someone who kills it, he owes the jaza (a compensation). It is the same whether he did it on purpose or forgot, and whether it is his first time or he has done it before.

cards.ask: Nasir forgets he is in ihram and kills a rabbit. What does he owe?
options: The jaza, the same as if on purpose
cards.source: يستوي في ذلك العامد والناسي
cards.why: Forgetting and doing it on purpose are the same: the jaza is owed.

cards.title: Valuing the animal
cards.ar: والجزاء عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف أن يقوم الصيد في المكان الذي قتله فيه أو في أقرب المواضع منه إن كان في برية يقومه ذوا عدل
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf, the jaza is the animal's value in the place it was killed, or the nearest place to it if it was in open desert. Two fair men set the value. Note: Muhammad says that where an animal has a match among livestock, that match is owed (a sheep for a gazelle, a badana for an ostrich).

cards.title: His choice with the value
cards.ar: ثم هو مخير في القيمة إن شاء ابتاع بها هديا وإن شاء اشترى بها طعاما فتصدق به على كل مسكين
cards.en: Then he chooses what to do with the value: buy a hady (an animal to sacrifice) with it; or buy food and give each poor person half a sa' of wheat or a sa' of dates or barley; or fast.

cards.ask: Complete it: what may he buy with the value?
cards.ar: إن شاء ابتاع بها ____
cards.source: إن شاء ابتاع بها هديا
cards.why: He may buy a hady with the value, to be sacrificed.

cards.title: Fasting for it
cards.ar: وإن شاء صام عن كل نصف صاع من بر يوما وعن كل صاع من شعير يوما فإن فضل من الطعام أقل من نصف صاع فهو مخير: إن شاء تصدق به وإن شاء صام عنه يوما كاملا
cards.en: Or he fasts one day for each half sa' of wheat, or each sa' of barley, that the value would buy. If less than half a sa' is left over, he chooses: give it in charity, or fast a whole day for it.

cards.ask: The animal Hamza killed is valued at enough to buy 5 sa' of wheat. He chooses to fast. How many days?
cards.source: وإن شاء صام عن كل نصف صاع من بر يوما
cards.why: One day for every half sa' of wheat: 5 sa' is 10 half-sa's, so 10 days.

cards.ask: After fasting, a quarter sa' of wheat is left over from Bilal's jaza. What does he do?
options: Give it in charity, or fast a whole day: his choice
Nothing: less than half a sa' is dropped
cards.source: فإن فضل من الطعام أقل من نصف صاع فهو مخير: إن شاء تصدق به وإن شاء صام عنه يوما كاملا
cards.why: A leftover of less than half a sa' can be given away, or he fasts a full day for it.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Showing game to a hunter who kills it means a jaza
Two fair men value the animal
He may fast instead of giving food
A second offence needs no jaza
The value is always taken in Makkah

source: أو دل عليه من قتله فعليه الجزاء
يقومه ذوا عدل
وإن شاء صام
والمبتدئ والعائد
في المكان الذي قتله فيه
cards.why: Showing it counts, two fair men value it, and fasting is allowed. A repeat offence is the same, and the value is where it was killed.

lessons.title: Wounding game, and what is free to kill

cards.title: Wounding
cards.ar: ومن جرح صيدا أو نتف شعره أو قطع عضوا منه ضمن ما نقصه وإن نتف ريش طائر أو قطع قوائم صيد فخرج من حيز الامتناع فعليه قيمته كاملة
cards.en: Whoever wounds game, pulls out its hair or cuts off a part pays for the value it lost. If he plucks a bird's feathers, or cuts an animal's legs, so that it can no longer escape, he owes its full value.

cards.ask: Yasir, in ihram, plucks a pigeon's flight feathers so it can no longer fly away. What does he owe?
cards.source: وإن نتف ريش طائر أو قطع قوائم صيد فخرج من حيز الامتناع فعليه قيمته كاملة
cards.why: It can no longer escape, so he owes its full value.

cards.title: Eggs
cards.ar: ومن كسر بيض صيد فعليه قيمته فإن خرج من البيض فرخ ميت فعليه قيمته حيا
cards.en: Whoever breaks the egg of a wild bird owes its value. If a dead chick comes out of it, he owes the chick's value as if alive.

cards.ask: Umar breaks an ostrich egg and a dead chick is inside. What does he owe?
options: The value of the chick alive
The value of the egg only
cards.source: فإن خرج من البيض فرخ ميت فعليه قيمته حيا
cards.why: A dead chick from the egg means its value as a living chick.

cards.title: Animals with no jaza
cards.ar: وليس في قتل الغراب والحدأة والذئب والحية والعقرب والفأرة جزاء وليس في قتل البعوض والبراغيث والقراد شيء
cards.en: There is no jaza for killing a crow, a kite (bird of prey), a wolf, a snake, a scorpion or a mouse. Nothing is owed for mosquitoes, fleas or ticks.

cards.title: Lice and locusts
cards.ar: ومن قتل قملة تصدق بما شاء ومن قتل جرادة تصدق بما شاء وتمرة خير من جرادة
cards.en: Whoever kills a louse gives whatever charity he likes. Whoever kills a locust gives whatever charity he likes, and a date is better than a locust.

cards.ask: What does the muhrim owe for killing it?
source: وليس في قتل الغراب والحدأة والذئب والحية والعقرب والفأرة جزاء
وليس في قتل البعوض والبراغيث والقراد شيء
ومن قتل قملة تصدق بما شاء ومن قتل جرادة تصدق بما شاء
وإذا قتل المحرم صيدا
cards.why: Game like a gazelle needs the jaza. A louse or locust: any small charity. A scorpion, wolf or mosquito: nothing.

cards.title: Predators
cards.ar: ومن قتل ما لا يؤكل لحمه من الصيد كالسباع ونحوها فعليه الجزاء ولا يتجاوز بقيمتها شاة
cards.en: Whoever kills game whose meat is not eaten, like wild predators, owes the jaza, but its value is not taken above that of a sheep.

cards.ask: Sa'd, in ihram, kills a wild cat (a predator) that is valued at more than a sheep. It did not attack him. What does he owe?
options: The jaza, but no more than a sheep's value
Its full value, whatever it is
Nothing: its meat is not eaten
cards.source: فعليه الجزاء ولا يتجاوز بقيمتها شاة
cards.why: A predator still needs a jaza, capped at the value of a sheep.

cards.ask: Complete it: what is better than a locust?
cards.ar: و____ خير من جرادة
cards.source: وتمرة خير من جرادة
cards.why: "A date is better than a locust": a small charity is enough.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Wounding game: pay the value it lost
Killing a snake: no jaza
Killing a predator: a jaza up to a sheep
Killing a flea: a sheep
Breaking an egg: nothing

source: ضمن ما نقصه
والحية
ولا يتجاوز بقيمتها شاة
والبراغيث
ومن كسر بيض صيد فعليه قيمته
cards.why: A wound costs what it took off, a snake is free, a predator is capped at a sheep. A flea costs nothing, and an egg costs its value.

cards.title: When a predator attacks
cards.ar: وإن صال السبع على محرم فقتله فلا شيء عليه
cards.en: If a wild predator attacks a muhrim and he kills it, he owes nothing.

cards.title: Need, and tame animals
cards.ar: وإن اضطر المحرم إلى أكل لحم الصيد فقتله فعليه الجزاء ولا بأس أن يذبح المحرم الشاة والبقرة والبعير والدجاج والبط الكسكري وإن قتل حماما مسرولا أو ظبيا مستأنسا فعليه الجزاء
cards.en: If he is forced by hunger to eat game and kills it, he owes the jaza. He may slaughter sheep, cows, camels, chickens and farm ducks. But if he kills a feather-legged pigeon or a tame gazelle, he owes the jaza: they are still game.

cards.ask: Does the muhrim owe a jaza?
items: Kills a wolf that attacks him
Kills a deer because he is starving
source: وإن صال السبع على محرم فقتله فلا شيء عليه
وإن اضطر المحرم إلى أكل لحم الصيد فقتله فعليه الجزاء
ولا بأس أن يذبح المحرم الشاة والبقرة والبعير والدجاج
أو ظبيا مستأنسا فعليه الجزاء
cards.why: An attacker and farm animals cost nothing. Game killed from hunger, and a tame gazelle, still need the jaza.

cards.ask: Idris is lost and starving in ihram. He kills a deer to eat. What is the ruling?
options: He may, but owes the jaza
He may not, even to survive
cards.source: وإن اضطر المحرم إلى أكل لحم الصيد فقتله فعليه الجزاء
cards.why: Need lets him do it, but the jaza is still owed.

cards.title: Game slaughtered by a muhrim
cards.ar: وإن ذبح المحرم صيدا فذبيحته ميتة لا يحل أكلها
cards.en: If a muhrim slaughters game, it counts as carrion (an animal that died without proper slaughter), and no one may eat it.

cards.ask: Zayd is not in ihram. He hunts a deer by himself and gives some meat to Umar, who is in ihram. Umar did not point it out or ask for it. May Umar eat it?
options: No: a muhrim may never eat game
cards.source: لحم صيد اصطاده أو ذبحه إذا لم يدله المحرم عليه ولا أمره بصيده
cards.why: A muhrim may eat game someone else hunted or slaughtered, as long as he did not point it out or order it.

cards.title: The Haram's game and plants
cards.ar: وفي صيد الحرم إذا ذبحه الحلال فعليه الجزاء وإن قطع حشيش الحرم أو شجره الذي ليس بمملوك ولا هو مما ينبته الناس فعليه قيمته
cards.en: Halal means not in ihram. If even a halal person slaughters game of the Haram, he owes the jaza. If he cuts the Haram's grass or trees, ones not owned and not of the kind people plant, he owes their value.

cards.ask: Salim, not in ihram, cuts down a wild tree growing in the Haram that nobody owns or planted. What does he owe?
options: Nothing: he is not in ihram
cards.source: وإن قطع حشيش الحرم أو شجره الذي ليس بمملوك ولا هو مما ينبته الناس فعليه قيمته
cards.why: The Haram's wild trees and grass are protected for everyone; cutting them means paying their value.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Game slaughtered by a muhrim is carrion
A halal person who kills Haram game owes the jaza
A muhrim may slaughter a camel
A tame gazelle is no longer game
A muhrim may eat game he pointed out to the hunter

source: فذبيحته ميتة لا يحل أكلها
وفي صيد الحرم إذا ذبحه الحلال فعليه الجزاء
والبعير
أو ظبيا مستأنسا فعليه الجزاء
إذا لم يدله المحرم عليه
cards.why: His slaughter is carrion, Haram game is protected even from a halal person, and camels are fine. A tame gazelle still needs the jaza, and pointing it out makes the meat not allowed.

lessons.title: The qarin's double, sharing, and selling game

cards.title: Two dams for the qarin
cards.ar: وكل شيء فعله القارن مما ذكرنا أن فيه على المفرد دما فعليه دمان: دم لحجته ودم لعمرته
cards.en: For everything mentioned above where the mufrid owes one dam, the qarin owes two: one for his Hajj and one for his umrah.

cards.ask: Yasir is a qarin. He wears a shirt for a whole day. What does he owe?
source: فعليه دمان: دم لحجته ودم لعمرته
وإن لبس ثوبا مخيطا أو غطى رأسه يوما كاملا فعليه دم
cards.why: A mufrid would owe one dam, so the qarin owes two.

cards.title: Passing the miqat
cards.ar: إلا أن يتجاوز الميقات من غير إحرام ثم يحرم بالعمرة والحج فيلزمه دم واحد
cards.en: Except if he passes the miqat without ihram and then enters ihram for umrah and Hajj: then he owes one dam.

cards.ask: Khalid passes the miqat without ihram, then enters ihram for qiran. How many dams for passing the miqat?
cards.source: إلا أن يتجاوز الميقات من غير إحرام ثم يحرم بالعمرة والحج فيلزمه دم واحد
cards.why: This is the one exception: passing the miqat costs the qarin a single dam.

cards.title: Sharing a kill
cards.ar: وإذا اشترك المحرمان في قتل صيد فعلى كل واحد منهما الجزاء كاملا وإذا اشترك الحلالان في قتل صيد الحرم فعليهما جزاء واحد
cards.en: If two muhrims kill one animal together, each owes a full jaza. If two halal people together kill game of the Haram, they owe one jaza between them.

cards.ask: Ali and Umar, both in ihram, kill one deer together. What is owed?
cards.source: وإذا اشترك المحرمان في قتل صيد فعلى كل واحد منهما الجزاء كاملا
cards.why: Each muhrim owes a full jaza of his own.

cards.ask: Two men not in ihram kill one deer together inside the Haram. What is owed?
cards.source: وإذا اشترك الحلالان في قتل صيد الحرم فعليهما جزاء واحد
cards.why: For two halal people it is one jaza between them.

cards.title: Selling game
cards.ar: وإذا باع المحرم صيدا أو ابتاعه فالبيع باطل
cards.en: If a muhrim sells game or buys it, the sale is void.

cards.ask: Hamza, in ihram, buys a live gazelle at a market. What is the sale?
cards.source: وإذا باع المحرم صيدا أو ابتاعه فالبيع باطل
cards.why: A muhrim's sale or purchase of game is void.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The qarin owes double where the mufrid owes a dam
Two muhrims who share a kill each owe a full jaza
A muhrim's purchase of game is void
Two halal people sharing a Haram kill each owe a full jaza
Passing the miqat costs the qarin two dams

source: فعليه دمان
فعلى كل واحد منهما الجزاء كاملا
فالبيع باطل
فعليهما جزاء واحد
فيلزمه دم واحد
cards.why: Double for the qarin, a full jaza each for two muhrims, and the sale is void. Two halal people owe one jaza, and the miqat costs one dam.

cards.title: Coming out of ihram when held back
cards.ar: إذا أحصر المحرم بعدو أو أصابه مرض منعه من المضي جاز له التحلل وقيل له: ابعث شاة تذبح في الحرم وواعد من يحملها يوما بعينه يذبحها فيه ثم تحلل وإن كان قارنا بعث بدمين
cards.en: A muhsar is a pilgrim held back by an enemy or by an illness that stops him going on. He may come out of ihram. He sends a sheep to be slaughtered in the Haram, agrees a fixed day with whoever takes it, and comes out of ihram after that. A qarin sends two.

cards.ask: Bilal is in ihram for Hajj but falls so ill on the way that he cannot go on. What does he do?
options: Send a sheep to be slaughtered in the Haram on a set day, then leave ihram
Leave ihram at once with nothing owed
Stay in ihram until next year
cards.source: ابعث شاة تذبح في الحرم وواعد من يحملها يوما بعينه يذبحها فيه ثم تحلل
cards.why: Illness makes him a muhsar. He sends a sheep to the Haram for a set day, then comes out of ihram.

cards.title: Where and when
cards.ar: ولا يجوز ذبح دم الإحصار إلا في الحرم ويجوز ذبحه قبل يوم النحر عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: The dam of ihsar may only be slaughtered in the Haram. For Abu Hanifa it may be slaughtered before the Day of Sacrifice. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that for one held back from Hajj, it must be on the Day of Sacrifice.

cards.title: What he makes up
cards.ar: ويجوز للمحصر بالعمرة أن يذبح متى شاء والمحصر بالحج إذا تحلل فعليه حجة وعمرة وعلى المحصر بالعمرة القضاء وعلى القارن حجة وعمرتان
cards.en: One held back from an umrah may slaughter whenever he likes. One held back from Hajj who comes out of ihram owes a Hajj and an umrah. One held back from an umrah makes it up. A qarin owes a Hajj and two umrahs.

cards.ask: Umar was a qarin and was held back by an enemy. He came out of ihram. What does he owe later?
cards.source: وعلى القارن حجة وعمرتان
cards.why: The qarin who is held back owes a Hajj and two umrahs.

cards.ask: Sa'd was held back from Hajj (not qiran) and came out of ihram. What does he owe?
cards.source: والمحصر بالحج إذا تحلل فعليه حجة وعمرة
cards.why: One held back from Hajj owes a Hajj and an umrah.

cards.title: If the hold-up ends
cards.ar: ثم زال الإحصار فإن قدر على إدراك الهدي والحج لم يجز له التحلل ولزمه المضي وإن قدر على إدراك الهدي دون الحج تحلل وإن قدر على إدراك الحج دون الهدي جاز له التحلل استحسانا
cards.en: If he has sent the hady and then the hold-up ends: if he can reach both the hady and the Hajj, he may not come out of ihram and must go on. If he can reach the hady but not the Hajj, he comes out of ihram. If he can reach the Hajj but not the hady, he may come out of ihram, by istihsan (a ruling made on preference for a stronger reason).

cards.ask: Yusuf's illness ends after he sent his hady. He can catch up with the hady and still reach the Hajj in time. What must he do?
options: Go on with his Hajj; he may not leave ihram
cards.source: فإن قدر على إدراك الهدي والحج لم يجز له التحلل ولزمه المضي
cards.why: If both the hady and the Hajj can be reached, he must carry on.

cards.title: Held back in Makkah
cards.ar: بمكة وهو ممنوع من الوقوف والطواف كان محصرا وإن قدر على إحدهما فليس بمحصر
cards.en: Someone held back in Makkah is a muhsar if he is barred from both the standing at Arafa and the tawaf. If he can do either one, he is not a muhsar.

cards.ask: Hassan is in Makkah. He is barred from going to Arafat, but can do tawaf. Is he a muhsar?
options: No: he can still do one of them
Yes: he cannot stand at Arafa
Yes, if he sends a hady
cards.source: وإن قدر على إحدهما فليس بمحصر
cards.why: He is only a muhsar if barred from both. He can do the tawaf, so he is not.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Illness can make someone a muhsar
The dam of ihsar is slaughtered only in the Haram
A qarin who is held back sends two dams
One held back from umrah must wait for the Day of Sacrifice to slaughter
Someone barred only from Arafat in Makkah is a muhsar

source: أو أصابه مرض منعه من المضي
ولا يجوز ذبح دم الإحصار إلا في الحرم
وإن كان قارنا بعث بدمين
ويجوز للمحصر بالعمرة أن يذبح متى شاء
وإن قدر على إحدهما فليس بمحصر
cards.why: Illness counts, the slaughter is in the Haram, and a qarin sends two. Umrah's dam may be any time, and one barred from only one of the two is not a muhsar.

lessons.title: Missing the Hajj, and the umrah

cards.title: Missing the standing
cards.ar: ومن أحرم بالحج ففاته الوقوف بعرفة حتى طلع الفجر من يوم النحر فقد فاته الحج وعليه أن يطوف ويسعى ويتحلل ويقضي الحج من قابل ولا دم عليه
cards.en: Whoever is in ihram for Hajj but misses the standing at Arafa until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice has missed the Hajj. He does tawaf and sa'y, comes out of ihram, and makes up the Hajj the next year. He owes no dam.

cards.ask: Musa reaches Arafat after dawn on the Day of Sacrifice. What does he do?
options: Tawaf and sa'y, leave ihram, and do Hajj next year; no dam
Stay in ihram until next year's Arafa
cards.source: فقد فاته الحج وعليه أن يطوف ويسعى ويتحلل ويقضي الحج من قابل ولا دم عليه
cards.why: After dawn of the Day of Sacrifice the Hajj is missed. He leaves ihram with tawaf and sa'y and makes it up next year, with no dam.

cards.title: The umrah cannot be missed
cards.ar: والعمرة لا تفوت وهي جائزة في جميع السنة إلا خمسة أيام يكره فعلها فيها: يوم عرفة ويوم النحر وأيام التشريق
cards.en: An umrah can never be missed. It may be done all year round, except on five days when it is makruh: the Day of Arafa, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashriq (the three days after the Day of Sacrifice).

cards.ask: Complete it: on how many days is umrah makruh?
cards.ar: إلا ____ أيام يكره فعلها فيها
cards.source: إلا خمسة أيام يكره فعلها فيها
cards.why: Five: the Day of Arafa, the Day of Sacrifice, and the three Days of Tashriq.

cards.ask: Is umrah makruh on this day?
cards.source: وهي جائزة في جميع السنة إلا خمسة أيام يكره فعلها فيها: يوم عرفة ويوم النحر وأيام التشريق
cards.why: It is fine all year except Arafa, the Day of Sacrifice and the Days of Tashriq.

cards.title: What umrah is
cards.ar: والعمرة سنة وهي: الإحرام والطواف والسعي والحلق أو التقصير
cards.en: Umrah is sunnah. It is: ihram, tawaf, sa'y, and shaving or cutting the hair.

cards.ask: Put the umrah in order.
cards.source: والعمرة سنة وهي: الإحرام والطواف والسعي والحلق أو التقصير
cards.why: Ihram, then tawaf, then sa'y, then shaving or cutting.

cards.ask: Zaynab wants to do an umrah on the 12th of Dhul-Hijja, a Day of Tashriq. What is the ruling?
options: Fine: it is after the Day of Sacrifice
cards.source: يوم عرفة ويوم النحر وأيام التشريق
cards.why: The Days of Tashriq are among the five days when umrah is makruh.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Umrah is sunnah
Whoever misses the Hajj owes no dam
Umrah cannot be missed
Umrah is makruh in all of Dhul-Hijja
Whoever misses Arafa stays in ihram until next year

source: والعمرة سنة
ولا دم عليه
والعمرة لا تفوت
إلا خمسة أيام
وعليه أن يطوف ويسعى ويتحلل
cards.why: Umrah is sunnah and cannot be missed, and missing the Hajj costs no dam. Only five days are makruh, and he comes out of ihram with tawaf and sa'y.

cards.title: What a hady can be
cards.ar: الهدي: أدناه شاة وهو من ثلاثة نوع: الإبل والبقر والغنم يجزئ في ذلك الثني فصاعدا إلا من الضأن فإن الجذع منه يجزئ
cards.en: The least a hady can be is a sheep or goat. It comes from three kinds: camels, cattle, and sheep or goats. A thani (an animal grown to a set age) or older is valid, except that from sheep (da'n) a jadha' (a younger one) is enough.

cards.ask: Which animals can be a hady?

options.text: A camel
A cow
A goat
A chicken
A deer

cards.source: وهو من ثلاثة نوع: الإبل والبقر والغنم
cards.why: Only camels, cattle and sheep or goats. Chickens and deer are not among the three.

cards.title: Faults that rule it out
cards.ar: ولا يجوز في الهدي مقطوع الأذن أو أكثرها ولا مقطوع الذنب ولا اليد ولا الرجل ولا الذاهبة العين ولا العجفاء ولا العرجاء التي لا تمشي إلى
cards.en: Not valid as a hady: one with its ear, or most of it, cut off; one with its tail, foreleg or hind leg cut off; one that has lost an eye; a very thin one; or one so lame it cannot walk to the place of sacrifice.

cards.ask: Ibrahim's sheep has lost one eye. Can it be his hady?
options: Yes: an eye is a small fault
cards.source: ولا الذاهبة العين
cards.why: An animal that has lost an eye is not valid as a hady.

cards.title: When only a badana will do
cards.ar: والشاة جائزة في كل شيء إلا في موضعين: من طاف طواف الزيارة جنبا ومن جامع بعد الوقوف بعرفة فإنه لا يجوز إلا بدنة
cards.en: A sheep is enough for everything except two cases: whoever did tawaf al-ziyara while junub, and whoever had intercourse after the standing at Arafa. For these, only a badana will do.

cards.ask: Which of these needs a badana, not a sheep?
options: Intercourse after the standing at Arafa
Shaving a quarter of the head
cards.source: ومن جامع بعد الوقوف بعرفة فإنه لا يجوز إلا بدنة
cards.why: Intercourse after Arafa is one of the two cases that need a badana. The others are a sheep.

cards.title: Seven sharing
cards.ar: والبدنة والبقرة تجزئ كل واحدة منهما عن سبعة إذا كان كل واحد من الشركاء يريد القربة فإن أراد أحدهم بنصيبه اللحم لم يجزئ عن الباقين
cards.en: A badana or a cow counts for seven people, as long as each partner means it as worship (to draw near to Allah). If one of them only wants the meat for his share, it does not count for the others.

cards.ask: Seven men share a cow as a hady. One of them only wants the meat for his family's dinner. What is the ruling?
options: It counts for none of them
It counts for the six others
cards.source: فإن أراد أحدهم بنصيبه اللحم لم يجزئ عن الباقين
cards.why: If one partner wants only meat, it does not count for the rest.

cards.title: Eating from it
cards.ar: ويجوز الأكل من هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران ولا يجوز الأكل من بقية الهدايا
cards.en: He may eat from a voluntary hady, and from the hady of tamattu' and qiran. He may not eat from any other hady.

cards.ask: May he eat from it?
items: A dam for wearing a shirt all day
cards.source: ويجوز الأكل من هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران ولا يجوز الأكل من بقية الهدايا
cards.why: Only the voluntary, tamattu' and qiran hadys may be eaten from. Penalty dams and the rest may not.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The least hady is a sheep or goat
A young jadha' sheep is valid
A cow counts for seven
A very thin animal is valid
He may eat from the badana for al-ziyara while junub

source: الهدي: أدناه شاة
فإن الجذع منه يجزئ
تجزئ كل واحدة منهما عن سبعة
ولا العجفاء
ولا يجوز الأكل من بقية الهدايا
cards.why: A sheep is the least, a jadha' sheep is fine, and a cow covers seven. A thin animal is not valid, and a penalty badana is not eaten from.

lessons.title: Slaughtering and caring for the hady

cards.title: When and where
cards.ar: ولا يجوز ذبح هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران إلا في يوم النحر ويجوز ذبح بقية الهدايا أي وقت شاء ولا يجوز ذبح الهدايا إلا في الحرم ويجوز أن يتصدق بها على مساكين الحرم وغيرهم ولا يجب التعريف بالهدايا
cards.en: The voluntary, tamattu' and qiran hadys may only be slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice. The others may be slaughtered any time. Every hady must be slaughtered in the Haram. Its meat may be given to the poor of the Haram or others. Ta'rif (taking the hady to Arafat) is not required.

cards.ask: Ali is doing tamattu'. He wants to slaughter his hady on the 7th of Dhul-Hijja to get it done. May he?
options: No: only on the Day of Sacrifice
Yes, if it is in the Haram
cards.source: ولا يجوز ذبح هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران إلا في يوم النحر
cards.why: The tamattu' hady may only be slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice.

cards.title: Nahr, dhabh, and doing it himself
cards.ar: والأفضل في البدن النحر وفي البقر والغنم الذبح والأولى أن يتولى الإنسان ذبحها بنفسه إذا كان يحسن ذلك ويتصدق بجلالها وخطامها ولا يعطي أجرة الجزار منها
cards.en: For camels, nahr (a stab at the base of the neck) is best; for cattle and sheep, dhabh (cutting the throat). It is best to slaughter it himself if he does it well. He gives away its covering cloth and halter in charity, and does not pay the butcher from it.

cards.ask: Hamid wants to pay the butcher with the hide and some meat of his hady. May he?
options: No: the butcher's pay may not come from it
cards.source: ولا يعطي أجرة الجزار منها
cards.why: The butcher's wage must not be paid from the hady.

cards.title: Riding and milk
cards.ar: ومن ساق بدنة فاضطر إلى ركوبها ركبها وإن استغنى عن ذلك لم يركبها وإن كان لها لبن لم يحلبها وينضح ضرعها بالماء البارد حتى ينقطع اللبن
cards.en: Whoever drives a badana may ride it if he has to, but not if he can do without. If it has milk, he does not milk it, but splashes its udder with cold water until the milk stops.

cards.ask: Sulayman's hady camel has milk. What does he do?
options: Not milk it, but splash its udder with cold water
Milk it and drink the milk
Milk it and give the milk away
cards.source: وإن كان لها لبن لم يحلبها وينضح ضرعها بالماء البارد حتى ينقطع اللبن
cards.why: He leaves the milk and cools the udder with cold water until it stops.

cards.title: If it dies or is damaged
cards.ar: ومن ساق هديا فعطب فإن كان تطوعا فليس عليه غيره وإن كان عن واجب فعليه أن يقيم غيره مقامه وإن أصابه عيب كبير أقام غيره مقامه
cards.en: If a hady he is driving perishes: if it was voluntary, he owes no other. If it was owed, he must put another in its place. If it gets a big fault, he puts another in its place.

cards.title: If it is dying on the road
cards.ar: ما شاء وإذا عطبت البدنة في الطريق فإن كان تطوعا نحرها وصبغ نعلها بدمها وضرب بها صفحتها ولا يأكل منها هو ولا غيره من الأغنياء وإن كانت واجبة أقام غيرها مقامها وصنع بها ما شاء
cards.en: He may do what he likes with the faulty one. If a badana is dying on the road: if it was voluntary, he slaughters it, dips its sandal-garland in its blood and strikes its side with it (so people know it is a hady). Neither he nor any rich person eats from it. If it was owed, he puts another in its place and does what he likes with this one.

cards.ask: Yasir's voluntary hady camel collapses and is dying on the road. What does he do?
options: Slaughter it, mark it with its blood, and leave it; he and the rich do not eat
Slaughter it and eat it himself
Buy another and keep this one
cards.source: فإن كان تطوعا نحرها وصبغ نعلها بدمها وضرب بها صفحتها ولا يأكل منها هو ولا غيره من الأغنياء
cards.why: A voluntary one is slaughtered and marked; he and the wealthy do not eat from it.

cards.title: Which hadys are garlanded
cards.ar: ويقلد هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران ولا يقلد دم الإحصار ولا دم الجنايات
cards.en: The voluntary, tamattu' and qiran hadys are garlanded. The dam of ihsar and the dams for wrongs are not.

cards.ask: Garlanded or not?
items: A dam for perfume in ihram
cards.source: ويقلد هدي التطوع والمتعة والقران ولا يقلد دم الإحصار ولا دم الجنايات
cards.why: Voluntary, tamattu' and qiran hadys are garlanded; dams for ihsar and wrongs are not.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: Every hady is slaughtered in the Haram
Taking the hady to Arafat is not required
Nahr is best for camels
A voluntary hady that perishes must be replaced
He may ride his badana whenever he likes

source: ولا يجوز ذبح الهدايا إلا في الحرم
ولا يجب التعريف بالهدايا
والأفضل في البدن النحر
فإن كان تطوعا فليس عليه غيره
وإن استغنى عن ذلك لم يركبها
cards.why: All in the Haram, no ta'rif needed, and nahr for camels. A voluntary one needs no replacement, and he rides only when he must.

lessons.title: Making a sale: offer and acceptance

cards.title: Offer and acceptance
cards.ar: البيع: ينعقد بالإيجاب والقبول إذا كانا بلفظ الماضي
cards.en: A sale (bay') is made by an offer (ijab) and an acceptance (qabul), when both are said in the past tense: "I have sold it to you", "I have bought it." Words like these show the deal is done, not just planned.

cards.ask: Zaid says, "I will sell you my bike for £50." Omar answers, "I will buy it." Has a sale been made?
options: No: the words must be in the past tense
Yes, as soon as they shake hands
cards.source: البيع: ينعقد بالإيجاب والقبول إذا كانا بلفظ الماضي
cards.why: "I will sell" and "I will buy" are promises about the future. The sale is made when offer and acceptance are in the past tense.

cards.title: Accept while you are still sitting
cards.ar: وإذا أوجب أحد المتعاقدين البيع فالآخر بالخيار: إن شاء قبل في المجلس وإن شاء رده وأيهما قام من المجلس قبل القبول بطل الإيجاب
cards.en: Once one side makes the offer, the other may accept or refuse while they are still in the same sitting (majlis), the meeting where the deal is being made. If either of them gets up and leaves before accepting, the offer is cancelled.

cards.ask: Aisha offers Sara her old laptop for £200 at a café. Sara stands up and walks out to think. An hour later she comes back and says, "I accept." Is there a sale?
options: No: the offer ended when she left the sitting
Yes: she accepted the same day
Yes, but only if Aisha repeats the price
cards.source: وأيهما قام من المجلس قبل القبول بطل الإيجاب
cards.why: Whoever leaves the sitting before accepting cancels the offer. Aisha would have to offer again.

cards.title: Once agreed, the sale is binding
cards.ar: وإذا حصل الإيجاب والقبول لزم البيع ولا خيار لواحد منهما إلا من عيب أو عدم رؤية
cards.en: When the offer and acceptance have both happened, the sale is binding: neither side can back out. A khiyar is an "option", a right to cancel. Here there is none, except for a defect in the item or for not having seen it.

cards.ask: Bilal buys a phone from a shop, and both say the words of sale. The next day he finds a cheaper one and wants his money back. Must the shop cancel?
options: Yes: anyone may cancel within three days
Yes, as long as the shop hasn't spent the money
cards.source: وإذا حصل الإيجاب والقبول لزم البيع ولا خيار لواحد منهما إلا من عيب أو عدم رؤية
cards.why: After offer and acceptance the sale is binding. Finding a better price is not a defect, and he saw the phone.

cards.title: A price must be known
cards.ar: والأعواض المشار إليها لا يحتاج إلى معرفة مقدراها في جواز البيع والأثمان المطلقة لا تصح إلا أن تكون معروفة القدر والصفة
cards.en: If the goods or payment are right there and pointed at ("this pile for that bag of coins"), their exact amount need not be known. But a price that is only named, not pointed at, must have a known amount and a known kind.

cards.title: Paying now or later
cards.ar: ويجوز البيع بثمن حال ومؤجل إذا كان الأجل معلوما ومن أطلق الثمن في البيع كان على غالب نقد البلد فإن كانت النقود مختلفة فالبيع فاسد إلا أن يبين أحدها
cards.en: The price may be paid now or later, if the date is known. If the price is named with no currency ("100"), it means the main currency of the town. If several currencies are used, the sale is fasid (invalid and not to be kept) unless one of them is named.

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's rule for paying later.
cards.ar: ويجوز البيع بثمن حال ومؤجل إذا كان الأجل ____
cards.source: ويجوز البيع بثمن حال ومؤجل إذا كان الأجل معلوما
cards.why: معلوما: the date to pay must be known. Short or written down is not the condition.

cards.ask: Hamza buys a sofa for £600 and says he will pay "whenever I get some money." Is that payment term allowed?
options: No: the date to pay is not known
Yes: any delay is fine between friends
Yes, if he pays within a year
cards.source: ويجوز البيع بثمن حال ومؤجل إذا كان الأجل معلوما
cards.why: Paying later is allowed only when the date is known. "Whenever I get money" is not a known date.

cards.ask: In a town where two currencies are used side by side, Yusuf sells his car "for 1000" and names neither. What is the sale?
options: Fasid, unless they name one currency
Valid, and the buyer picks the currency
cards.source: فإن كانت النقود مختلفة فالبيع فاسد إلا أن يبين أحدها
cards.why: With different currencies in use and none named, the price is unknown, so the sale is fasid until one is named.

cards.ask: Which of these are true?

options.text: A sale is made by offer and acceptance
The other side may accept while still in the sitting
After acceptance, either side may cancel for any reason
The price may be paid later, by a known date
A price of "some money" is fine

source: البيع: ينعقد بالإيجاب والقبول
إن شاء قبل في المجلس
لزم البيع ولا خيار لواحد منهما إلا من عيب أو عدم رؤية
والأثمان المطلقة لا تصح إلا أن تكون معروفة القدر والصفة
cards.why: Offer and acceptance make the sale, acceptance can come within the sitting, and a deferred price needs a known date. After that the sale is binding, and a vague price is not valid.

lessons.title: Selling by measure: heaps, flocks and cloth

cards.title: Measured, or by the heap
cards.ar: ويجوز بيع الطعام والحبوب مكايلة ومجازفة وبإناء بعينه لا يعرف مقدراه وبوزن حجر بعينه لا يعرف مقداره
cards.en: Food and grain may be sold measured out (mukayala), or as a heap judged by eye without measuring (mujazafa). They may also be sold by a particular container, or weighed against a particular stone, even if nobody knows its exact size.

cards.ask: A grocer sells "this whole sack of rice for £20" without weighing it. Is the sale valid?
options: Yes: grain may be sold by the heap
No: it must be weighed first
Only if the buyer weighs it at home
cards.source: ويجوز بيع الطعام والحبوب مكايلة ومجازفة
cards.why: Mujazafa, selling a heap by sight, is allowed for food and grain.

cards.title: "A dirham for each"
cards.ar: ومن باع صبرة طعام كل قفيز بدرهم جاز البيع في قفيز واحد عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يسمي جملة قفزانها ومن باع قطيع غنم كل شاة بدرهم فالبيع فاسد في جميعها
cards.en: A qafiz is a measure of grain, and a dirham is a silver coin. If someone sells a heap at "a dirham per qafiz" without saying how many qafiz there are, Abu Hanifa says the sale holds for one qafiz only, unless the total is named. A flock of sheep at "a dirham per sheep" is fasid for all of them.

cards.ask: A farmer sells "this flock, £100 a sheep" but nobody counts the sheep or names the total. What happens?
options: The sale is fasid for all of them
It is valid for one sheep
It is valid for the whole flock
cards.source: ومن باع قطيع غنم كل شاة بدرهم فالبيع فاسد في جميعها
cards.why: For a flock sold per head with no total, the sale is fasid in all of it. The one-unit rule is for a heap of food.

cards.ask: Under Abu Hanifa's rule, a shop sells "this heap of wheat, a dirham per qafiz" and names no total. For how much is the sale valid?
cards.source: جاز البيع في قفيز واحد عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يسمي جملة قفزانها
cards.why: Abu Hanifa holds it valid in one qafiz only, unless the total number of qafiz is named.

cards.title: A heap that turns out short
cards.ar: ومن ابتاع صبرة على أنها قفيز بمائة درهم فوجدها أقل كان المشتري بالخيار: إن شاء أخذ الموجود بحصته من الثمن وإن شاء فسخ البيع وإن وجدها أكثر فالزيادة للبائع
cards.en: If a heap is bought as being a stated amount for a stated price and it turns out less, the buyer chooses: take what is there for its share of the price, or cancel. If it turns out more, the extra belongs to the seller.

cards.ask: Maryam buys a sack "of 50 kg for £50". At home it is only 40 kg. What may she do?
options: Keep the 40 kg for £40, or cancel
cards.source: إن شاء أخذ الموجود بحصته من الثمن وإن شاء فسخ البيع
cards.why: For food sold by amount, the buyer takes what is there for its share of the price, or cancels the sale.

cards.title: Cloth and land are different
cards.ar: ومن اشترى ثوبا على أنه عشرة أذرع بعشرة دراهم أو أرضا على أنها مائة ذراع بمائة درهم فوجدها أقل فالمشتري بالخيار: إن شاء أخذها بجملة الثمن وإن شاء تركها وإن وجدها أكثر من الذراع الذي سماه فهو المشتري ولا خيار للبائع
cards.en: A dhira' (cubit) is an arm's length. For cloth or land sold at one lump price as "ten cubits", the length is only a description. If it is shorter, the buyer takes it for the full price or leaves it. If it is longer, the extra is the buyer's, and the seller has no option.

cards.title: When each cubit has its own price
cards.ar: وإن قال: بعتكها على أنها مائة ذراع بمائة درهم كل ذراع بدرهم فوجدها ناقصة
cards.en: But if the seller says "a hundred cubits for a hundred dirhams, a dirham per cubit", each cubit has its price. If it is short, the buyer may take it for its share of the price or leave it. If it is longer, the buyer may take all of it at a dirham a cubit, or cancel.

cards.ask: Land is sold as "100 cubits for 100 dirhams, a dirham per cubit". It measures 110 cubits. What are the buyer's choices?
options: Take all 110 for 110 dirhams, or cancel
source: وإن وجدها زائد كان المشتري بالخيار
كل ذراع بدرهم وإن شاء فسخ البيع
cards.why: Because each cubit was priced, the extra comes at a dirham each, so the buyer takes 110 for 110 or cancels.

cards.ask: The goods turn out bigger than stated. Who gets the extra?
items: A heap of wheat sold as an amount for a price
A sack of rice that weighs more than stated
Cloth sold as 10 cubits for 10 dirhams, lump price
Land sold as 100 cubits for 100 dirhams, lump price
source: وإن وجدها أكثر فالزيادة للبائع
وإن وجدها أكثر من الذراع الذي سماه فهو المشتري ولا خيار للبائع
cards.why: For food sold by amount, the extra is the seller's. For cloth or land at a lump price, length is a description, so the extra is the buyer's.

lessons.title: What comes with the sale, and who hands over first
lessons.arabic: ومن باع دارا دخل بناؤها في البيع

cards.title: A house and a plot
cards.ar: ومن باع دارا دخل بناؤها في البيع وإن لم يسمه
cards.en: Whoever sells a house sells its building with it, even if the building is not mentioned.

cards.title: Land, but not its crop
cards.ar: ومن باع أرضا دخل ما فيها وإن لم يسمه ولا يدخل الزرع في بيع الأرض إلا بالتسمية
cards.en: Land is sold with what is fixed in it, even if not mentioned. But a crop growing on it is not included unless it is named.

cards.ask: Khalid sells his farmland while a wheat crop is growing on it. Nothing is said about the crop. Whose is the wheat?
cards.source: ولا يدخل الزرع في بيع الأرض إلا بالتسمية
cards.why: A crop does not go with the land unless it is named in the sale.

cards.title: Fruit on the trees
cards.ar: ومن باع نخلا أو شجرا فيه ثمر فثمرته للبائع إلا أن يشترطها المبتاع ويقال للبائع: اقطعها وسلم المبيع
cards.en: If palms or trees are sold with fruit on them, the fruit stays the seller's, unless the buyer makes it a condition. The seller is told: pick your fruit and hand over what you sold.

cards.ask: Nadia buys an apple orchard in autumn. The trees are full of apples, and no one mentions them. What happens?
options: The apples are the seller's; he picks them and hands over the trees
The apples come with the trees
The apples are split in half
cards.source: فثمرته للبائع إلا أن يشترطها المبتاع ويقال للبائع: اقطعها وسلم المبيع
cards.why: Fruit on sold trees is the seller's unless the buyer made it a condition, so the seller picks it and hands over.

cards.title: Buying fruit still on the tree
cards.ar: ومن باع ثمرة لم يبد صلاحها أو قد بدا جاز البيع ووجب على المشتري قطعها في الحال فإن شرط تركها على النخل فسد البيع
cards.en: Fruit on the tree may be sold whether or not it has started to ripen, but the buyer must pick it straight away. If he makes it a condition to leave it on the tree, the sale is fasid.

cards.ask: Imran buys the mangoes on a neighbour's tree, "on condition they stay on the tree another month to ripen." What is the sale?
options: Valid, and the mangoes stay a month
Valid, but he pays extra rent
cards.source: فإن شرط تركها على النخل فسد البيع
cards.why: Leaving the fruit on the tree as a condition makes the sale fasid. Without it the buyer would pick them at once.

cards.title: Some things that are allowed and not
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن يبيع ثمرة ويستثني منها أرطالا معلومة ويجوز بيع الحنطة في سبيلها والباقلاء في قشرها ومن باع دارا دخل في المبيع مفاتيح أغلاقها
cards.en: A seller may not sell a fruit crop but keep back a set number of ratls (pounds) of it. Wheat still in the ear and beans in their pods may be sold. A house is sold with the keys to its locks.

cards.ask: Who pays this fee?
items: The man who measures out the grain
The man who checks the coins of the price
The man who weighs the coins of the price
cards.source: وأجرة الكيال وناقد الثمن على البائع وأجرة وزان الثمن على المشتري
cards.why: The measurer and the coin-checker are paid by the seller; the one who weighs the price is paid by the buyer.

cards.title: Who hands over first
cards.ar: ومن باع سلعة بثمن قيل للمشتري: ادفع الثمن أولا فإذا دفع قيل للبائع: سلم البيع ومن باع سلعة بسلعة أو ثمنا بثمن قيل لهما سلما معا
cards.en: When goods are sold for money, the buyer pays first, then the seller hands over the goods. When goods are swapped for goods, or money for money, both hand over together.

cards.ask: Ali swaps his games console for Sami's bike. Neither wants to go first. What is the rule?
cards.source: ومن باع سلعة بسلعة أو ثمنا بثمن قيل لهما سلما معا
cards.why: Goods for goods: both are told to hand over at the same time.

cards.ask: Without being mentioned, which come with the sale?

options.text: The building, with a house
The keys to the house's locks
A crop growing on the land
Fruit on the trees that are sold

source: ومن باع دارا دخل بناؤها في البيع وإن لم يسمه
ولا يدخل الزرع في بيع الأرض إلا بالتسمية
فثمرته للبائع إلا أن يشترطها المبتاع
دخل في المبيع مفاتيح أغلاقها
cards.why: The building and the keys come with a house. A crop and fruit on the trees stay the seller's unless named.

lessons.title: Option by condition: three days to decide

cards.title: Up to three days
cards.ar: خيار الشرط: جائز في البيع للبائع والمشتري ولهما الخيار ثلاثة أيام فما دونها ولا يجوز أكثر من ذلك عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد رحمهما الله: يجوز إذا سمى مدة معلومة
cards.en: Khiyar al-shart is an option by condition: the buyer or the seller keeps the right to cancel for a set time. It is allowed for three days or less, and Abu Hanifa does not allow more. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad allow a longer time if it is known.

cards.ask: Layla buys a dress "on condition I can cancel within three days." Is the condition allowed?
options: Yes: three days or less is allowed
No: a sale is binding at once
Only the seller may have an option
cards.source: جائز في البيع للبائع والمشتري ولهما الخيار ثلاثة أيام فما دونها
cards.why: Either side may have the option, for three days or less.

cards.ask: For Abu Hanifa, a buyer asks for "ten days to decide." Is that allowed?
options: No: not more than three days
Yes, any time they agree on
cards.source: ولا يجوز أكثر من ذلك عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: Abu Hanifa does not allow more than three days.

cards.title: Whose is the item meanwhile?
cards.ar: وخيار البائع يمنع خروج المبيع من ملكه فإن قبضه المشتري فهلك في يده
cards.en: If the seller has the option, the item stays his. If the buyer has taken it and it is destroyed with him, the buyer pays its value (qima: what it is worth), not the agreed price.

cards.title: When the buyer has the option
cards.ar: وخيار المشتري لا يمنع خروج المبيع من ملك البائع إلا أن المشتري لا يملكه عند أبي حنيفة وعندهما يملكه فإن هلك في يده هلك بالثمن وكذلك إن دخله عيب
cards.en: If the buyer has the option, the item leaves the seller's ownership, but for Abu Hanifa the buyer doesn't own it yet. If it is destroyed with the buyer, he pays the agreed price, and the same if it gets a defect. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the buyer does own it.

cards.ask: The item is destroyed in the buyer's hands. What does he pay?
items: The seller had the three-day option
The buyer had the three-day option
The buyer had the option, and it got a defect
source: بالقيمة وخيار المشتري لا يمنع خروج المبيع
فإن هلك في يده هلك بالثمن وكذلك إن دخله عيب
cards.why: With the seller's option the buyer pays its value. With the buyer's option it is lost at the agreed price, and a defect is the same.

cards.title: Approving and cancelling
cards.ar: ومن شرط له الخيار فله أن يفسخ في مدة الخيار وله أن يجيزه
cards.en: Whoever has the option may cancel the sale within the time, or approve it. He may approve it on his own, but he can cancel only when the other person is present.

cards.ask: Faris has a three-day option on a camera. While the seller is away, Faris says to himself, "I cancel." Does the cancellation count?
options: No: the other person must be present
Yes, if he sends the camera back
cards.source: وإن فسخ لم يجز إلا أن يكون الآخر حاضرا
cards.why: Approving needs no one else, but cancelling only counts with the other person present.

cards.title: If he dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات من له الخيار بطل خياره ولم ينتقل إلى ورثته
cards.en: If the person with the option dies, the option ends. It does not pass to his heirs.

cards.ask: Ibrahim buys a car with a three-day option and dies on day two. His sons want to cancel. Can they?
options: No: the option ended and didn't pass to them
Yes, but only on day three
cards.source: وإذا مات من له الخيار بطل خياره ولم ينتقل إلى ورثته
cards.why: The option ends with his death and is not inherited.

cards.ask: A slave was sold "as a baker" but cannot bake. What may the buyer do?
options: Take him for the full price, or leave him
Keep him and take back part of the price
cards.source: ومن باع عبدا على أنه خباز أو كاتب بخلاف ذلك فالمشتري بالخيار: إن شاء أخذه بجميع الثمن وإن شاء ترك
cards.why: When a described skill is missing, the buyer may take it at the full price or leave it.

cards.ask: Which are true of the option by condition?

options.text: The seller or the buyer may have it
Abu Hanifa allows up to three days
Cancelling needs the other person present
It passes to the heirs
Approving needs the other person present

source: خيار الشرط: جائز في البيع للبائع والمشتري
فإن أجازه بغير حضره صاحبه جاز وإن فسخ لم يجز إلا أن يكون الآخر حاضرا
ولم ينتقل إلى ورثته
cards.why: Either side may hold it for up to three days. Cancelling needs the other present, approving does not, and it ends at death.

cards.title: Buying what you haven't seen
cards.ar: شيئا لم يره فالبيع جائز وله الخيار إذا رآه: إن شاء أخذه وإن شاء
cards.en: Whoever buys something he hasn't seen, the sale is valid. When he sees it, he has khiyar al-ru'ya, the option of seeing: he may keep it or return it.

cards.ask: Adam orders a phone online without ever seeing it. When it arrives he doesn't like it. What may he do?
options: Keep it or return it: he has the option of seeing
Return it only if it is faulty
cards.source: شيئا لم يره فالبيع جائز وله الخيار إذا رآه
cards.why: The sale of an unseen item is valid, and the buyer gets an option once he sees it.

cards.title: No option for the seller
cards.ar: ومن باع ما لم يره فلا خيار له
cards.en: But whoever sells something he hasn't seen has no option.

cards.title: How much seeing is enough
cards.ar: ومن نظر إلى وجه الصبرة إلى ظاهر الثوب مطويا أو إلى وجه الجارية أو إلى وجه الدابة وكفلها فلا خيار له
cards.en: Seeing the main part is enough: the top of a heap of grain, the outside of folded cloth, the face of a slave girl, or the face and rump of an animal. After that there is no option. The same for seeing a house's courtyard, even without seeing its rooms.

cards.ask: Option of seeing or not?
items: A buyer who ordered a phone unseen
A seller who sold an inherited watch he never saw
A buyer who looked at the top of a sack of rice
A buyer who saw a house's courtyard but not its rooms
A buyer who saw a car last year and finds it rusted now
source: ومن باع ما لم يره فلا خيار له
ومن نظر إلى وجه الصبرة
وإن رأى صحن الدار فلا خيار له وإن لم يشاهد بيوتها
وإن وجده متغيرا فله الخيار
cards.why: The unseen buyer and the one who finds the item changed have the option. The seller never does, and seeing the top of the heap or the courtyard is enough.

cards.title: A blind buyer
cards.ar: وله الخيار إذا اشترى ويسقط خياره بأن يجس المبيع إذا كان يعرف بالجس أو يشمه إذا كان يعرف بالشم أو يذوقه إذا كان يعرف بالذوق ولا يسقط خياره في العقار حتى يوصف له
cards.en: A blind person may buy and sell, and when he buys he has the option. It ends when he feels the item, if it is known by feel; smells it, if known by smell; or tastes it, if known by taste. For land or a house it lasts until it is described to him.

cards.ask: Yaqub, who is blind, buys a bottle of perfume and smells it in the shop. Later he wants to return it. Does he still have the option?
options: No: smelling it ended his option
Yes: a blind buyer always keeps it
Yes, until someone describes it to him
cards.source: أو يشمه إذا كان يعرف بالشم
cards.why: Perfume is known by smell, so smelling it counts as seeing it and ends the option.

cards.title: Selling someone else's property
cards.ar: فالمالك بالخيار: إن شاء أجاز البيع وإن شاء فسخ وله الإجازة إذا كان المعقود عليه باقيا والمتعاقدان بحالهما
cards.en: If someone sells what belongs to another, the owner has the option: approve the sale or cancel it. He may approve only while the item still exists and both parties are as they were.

cards.ask: Your brother sells your bike without asking you. What is your right?
options: Approve the sale or cancel it
cards.source: فالمالك بالخيار: إن شاء أجاز البيع وإن شاء فسخ
cards.why: The owner chooses whether the sale stands.

cards.ask: Hana sees one of two shirts, buys both, then sees the second one. What may she do?
cards.source: ومن رأى أحد ثوبين فاشتراهما ثم رأى الآخر جاز له أن يردهما
cards.why: Her option of seeing covers the deal, so she may return both together.

cards.ask: Omar viewed a flat last month and buys it now. It is just as he saw it. Does he have the option of seeing?
options: No: it is as he saw it
Yes: he didn't see it on the day
source: ومن مات وله خيار الرؤية بطل خياره
ومن رأى شيئا ثم اشتراه بعد مدة: فإن كان على الصفة التي رآه فلا خيار له
cards.why: Seeing it earlier counts if nothing changed. (And if he had died with an option of seeing, it would end.)

cards.title: Keep it, or give it back
cards.ar: إن شاء أخذه بجميع الثمن وإن شاء رده وليس له أن يمسكه ويأخذ النقصان
cards.en: If the buyer finds an 'ayb (a defect), he chooses: keep it at the full price, or return it. He may not keep it and take back the difference (nuqsan, what the defect takes off the price).

cards.ask: Sara buys a phone and finds the screen was already cracked. She wants to keep it and get £50 back. Must the shop agree?
options: No: she keeps it at full price or returns it
Yes, if she asks within a week
source: إذا طلع المشتري على عيب في المبيع
وليس له أن يمسكه ويأخذ النقصان
cards.why: With a defect she may return it or keep it at the full price, but not keep it and take the difference.

cards.title: What counts as a defect
cards.ar: وكل ما أوجب نقصان الثمن في عادة التجار فهو عيب
cards.en: Anything that lowers the price in the custom of traders is a defect.

cards.ask: In the slaves of al-Quduri's time, which were defects?

options.text: Running away, in a young slave
Stealing, in a young slave
Bed-wetting in a grown slave, only from childhood and not since
Bad breath in a slave girl
Bad breath in a slave boy, if not from illness

source: والإباق والبول في الفراش والسرقة عيب في الصغير ما لم يبلغ
فليس ذلك بعيب حتى يعادوه بعد البلوغ والبخر والدفر عيب في الجارية وليس بعيب في الغلام إلا أن يكون من داء
والزنا وولد الزنا عيب في الجارية دون الغلام
cards.why: Running away, bed-wetting and stealing are defects in a child, but after adulthood only if they come back. Bad breath is a defect in a girl, and in a boy only if from illness: each lowers the price in traders' custom.

cards.title: A new defect at the buyer's
cards.ar: وإذا حدث عند المشتري عيب ثم اطلع على عيب كان عند البائع فله أن يرجع بنقصان العيب ولا يرد المبيع إلا أن يرضى البائع أن يأخذه بعيبه
cards.en: If the item gets a new defect with the buyer, and then he finds an old one from the seller, he claims the difference for the old defect. He can't return the item, unless the seller agrees to take it back with its new defect.

cards.ask: Zain scratches his new sofa, then finds a broken spring that was there before. What does he get?
options: The difference for the spring; he returns it only if the seller agrees
cards.source: فله أن يرجع بنقصان العيب ولا يرد المبيع إلا أن يرضى البائع أن يأخذه بعيبه
cards.why: With a new defect at the buyer's, he claims the difference for the old one and returns it only if the seller agrees.

cards.title: When the buyer changes it or uses it up
cards.ar: وإن قطع المشتري الثوب فوجد به عيبا رجع بالعيب وإن خاطه أو صبغه أو لت السويق بسمن ثم اطلع على عيب رجع بنقصانه وليس للبائع أن يأخذه ومن اشترى عبدا فأعتقه أو مات ثم اطلع على عيب رجع بنقصانه فإن قتل المشتري العبد أو كان طعاما فأكله لم يرجع عليه بشيء في قول أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يرجع
cards.en: If the buyer has cut, sewn or dyed the cloth, or mixed the barley flour with ghee, then finds a defect, he claims the difference, and the seller can't take it back. The same if he freed the slave or the slave died. But if he killed it, or it was food he ate, Abu Hanifa says he gets nothing. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he still claims the difference.

cards.ask: The buyer then finds an old defect. What does he get?
items: He had sewn the cloth into a shirt
It was food and he ate it (Abu Hanifa)
source: وإن خاطه أو صبغه
رجع بنقصانه وليس للبائع أن يأخذه
ومن اشترى عبدا فأعتقه أو مات ثم اطلع على عيب رجع بنقصانه
أو كان طعاما فأكله لم يرجع عليه بشيء في قول أبي حنيفة
cards.why: Sewing, dyeing and freeing keep his claim to the difference. Eating the food ends it for Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: Sold with no responsibility
cards.ar: ومن اشترى عبدا وشرط البراءة من كل عيب فليس له أن يرده بعيب وإن لم يسم العيوب ولم يعدها
cards.en: If the seller sells on condition that he is free of every defect (bara'a), the buyer can't return it for a defect, even if the defects were never named or listed.

cards.ask: Rashid sells his old car "free of responsibility for any defect." The buyer later finds a leaking engine. Can he return it?
options: No: the seller was freed from every defect
Yes: the leak was never named
cards.source: وشرط البراءة من كل عيب فليس له أن يرده بعيب وإن لم يسم العيوب ولم يعدها
cards.why: With a condition freeing him of every defect, no defect gives a return, named or not.

cards.ask: Musa bought a slave and sold him on. The second buyer returns him for a defect, and Musa takes him back without a judge's ruling. Can Musa now return him to his own seller?
options: No: he took him back without a judge
Yes, if the defect is serious
cards.source: فباعه المشتري ثم رد عليه بعيب فإن قبله بقضاء القاضي فله أن يرده على بائعه وإن قبله بغير قضاء القاضي فليس له أن يرده
cards.why: Only if he took it back by a judge's ruling may he pass it back to his seller. Taking it back by choice ends that.

cards.ask: Which buyer can still return the item for an old defect?
options: Huda, who found the defect before using it
Amir, who bought it "free of every defect"
Lina, who scratched it before finding the defect
source: إن شاء أخذه بجميع الثمن وإن شاء رده
وشرط البراءة من كل عيب فليس له أن يرده بعيب
ولا يرد المبيع إلا أن يرضى البائع
cards.why: Huda may return it. Amir agreed to no responsibility, and Lina added a new defect, so she only gets the difference unless the seller agrees.

lessons.title: Invalid sales 1: forbidden, not owned, not in hand

cards.title: Forbidden things
cards.ar: إذا كان أحد العوضين أو كلاهما محرما فالبيع فاسد كالبيع بالميتة أو بالدم أو بالخمر أو بالخنزير
cards.en: A fasid sale is a broken sale that must not stand. If one side of the deal, or both, is something haram (forbidden), the sale is fasid: like selling for carrion (an animal that died without slaughter), blood, wine or pork.

cards.ask: Tariq sells his car in exchange for a crate of wine. What is the sale?
options: Fasid: wine is a forbidden payment
Valid, since the car is halal
Valid, if the wine is poured away
cards.source: إذا كان أحد العوضين أو كلاهما محرما فالبيع فاسد
cards.why: If either side of the exchange is haram, the sale is fasid.

cards.title: What can't be owned
cards.ar: وكذلك إذا كان غير مملوك كالحر وبيع أم الولد والمدبر والمكاتب فاسد
cards.en: The same if the thing can't be owned and sold, like a free person. Also selling an umm walad (a slave woman who has had her master's child), a mudabbar (a slave promised freedom at the master's death) or a mukatab (a slave buying his freedom) is fasid.

cards.title: What isn't in hand
cards.ar: ولا يجوز بيع السمك في الماء ولا بيع الطير في الهواء ولا يجوز بيع الحمل ولا النتاج ولا بيع اللبن في الضرع
cards.en: You may not sell fish still in the water, a bird in the air, an unborn animal or the young it will have, or milk still in the udder.

cards.ask: Valid sale or invalid?
items: A heap of grain sold by sight
The fish swimming in a lake
The calf a cow is carrying
One cubit of a garment, still to be cut off
source: ويجوز بيع الطعام والحبوب مكايلة ومجازفة
ولا يجوز بيع السمك في الماء ولا بيع الطير في الهواء ولا يجوز بيع الحمل
وذراع من ثوب وجذع في سقف وضربة القانص
والباقلاء في قشرها
